Syllabus મુજબ વિગતવાર Theory, derivations, equipment ના Construction/Working તથા worked Numericals. Practical માં official suggested exercises તથા blank observation sheets છે—fabricated results નથી.
1. નોટ્સ
1.1 • Mass-transfer Operations તથા મહત્વ

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

યોગ્ય driving force હેઠળ mixture માં species નો relative transport અથવા phase boundary પાર transport એટલે Mass transfer. Components ને separate/recover કરવા આ transport વાપરતી process એટલે mass-transfer operation.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Separation માટે thermodynamic possibility તથા પૂરતો transfer rate બંને જોઈએ. Equilibrium attainable separation limit કરે છે; diffusion, contact area તથા time rate નક્કી કરે છે. Gas absorption, liquid extraction તથા solid માંથી soluble material dissolve કરવું examples છે. F ક્ત heat exchanger માં energy transfer અથવા unchanged mixture નું bulk transport selective mass separation નથી. Material balance quantities આપે છે; equilibrium તથા rate attainable compositions/equipment નક્કી કરે છે.

1.2 • Contacting Phases મુજબ Classification

વ્યાખ્યા

Selective component transfer માં ભાગ લેતી phases મુજબ classification થાય છે. Operation નું નામ separation mechanism પર પણ આધારિત છે.

Gas–liquid

Absorption માં soluble gas liquid માં જાય છે; stripping માં dissolved volatile component liquid માંથી gas માં જાય છે. Distillation માં vapor–liquid equilibrium તથા energy વડે volatile components redistribute થાય છે.

Liquid–liquid

સંપૂર્ણ mutually miscible ન હોય તેવી બે liquid phases વચ્ચે solute distribution એટલે extraction. Solvent થી ઉપયોગી selectivity તથા separable phases મળવા જોઈએ.

Solid–liquid તથા Solid–fluid

Leaching માં liquid solvent વડે solid માંનું soluble material dissolve થાય છે. Adsorption માં gas/liquid નો component solid surface પર accumulate થાય છે; તે bulk absorption નથી. Drying માં wet material નું moisture gas માં જાય છે; crystallization માં supersaturated liquid માંથી solid બને છે.

નોંધ

Membrane operations માટે selective barrier તથા driving force મુજબ વધારાનું classification થાય છે; bulk streams ને directly mix કરવી જરૂરી નથી. Related operations નો અહીં પરિચય છે; syllabus બહારની design derivations ઉમેરાતી નથી.

1.3 • Membrane Separation:Principle તથા Applications

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Selective barrier કેટલાક components ને preferentially pass કરીને બીજાં retain કરે તે membrane separation છે. Products permeate તથા retentate છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Module માં feed side, selective membrane તથા permeate side હોય છે. Selectivity pore size અથવા dense membrane માં sorption/diffusion થી મળી શકે છે. Pressure-driven microfiltration/ultrafiltration particles/macromolecules દૂર કરે છે. RO માં effective osmotic opposition કરતાં વધુ pressure થી dissolved salts મુખ્યત્વે દૂર થાય છે. Gas separation permeability/selectivity તથા partial-pressure difference વાપરે છે. Dialysis concentration/chemical-potential અને electrodialysis electric field તથા ion-selective membrane વાપરે છે. Water treatment, protein concentration તથા gas purification ઉપયોગો છે. Fouling, concentration polarization, compatibility, pretreatment, cleaning તથા energy performance limit કરે છે. નાના pores એટલે હંમેશાં perfect separation નહીં.

1.4 • Direct તથા Indirect Operations—Treybal Classification

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

આ classification માં heat ઉમેરવા/દૂર કરવાથી original solution માં separating phases ઉત્પન્ન થાય તે direct operation છે. Foreign separating substance ઉમેરાય તે indirect operation છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Classification: heat addition/removal થી fractional distillation તથા crystallization direct examples છે. Added solvent/gas/solid agent વાપરતાં absorption, stripping, liquid extraction, leaching તથા adsorption indirect examples છે. Direct methods માં foreign separating material ઉમેરાતું નથી, પણ energy વધુ લાગી શકે છે. Indirect methods ઉપયોગી selectivity આપે છે, પરંતુ agent recovery/loss, contamination તથા compatibility cost વધારી શકે છે. Product solution જ required હોય તો agent હંમેશાં દૂર કરવો જરૂરી નથી. Physical direct contact થી આ terminology જુદી છે. Packed absorber direct-contact device છે પણ textbook classification માં indirect operation છે.[1]

Reference: [1] Treybal, The Mass-Transfer Operations, Chapter1.

1.5 • Separation Method ની પસંદગી

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Purity, recovery, capacity તથા safety targets economical રીતે મેળવવા feasible operation તથા separating agent પસંદ કરવાં એટલે separation-method selection.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

પહેલાં feed phase, composition, flow તથા target products ઓળખો. Volatility, solubility, distribution, particle size અથવા membrane permeability નો ઉપયોગી difference શોધો. Equilibrium selectivity/driving force પછી rate, area તથા energy/solvent જરૂરિયાત જુઓ. Solvent recovery, contamination, thermal sensitivity, corrosion, toxicity, flammability, waste treatment તથા control flexibility ગણો. Regeneration મુશ્કેલ હોય તો સસ્તો solvent overall મોંઘો પડી શકે છે. High purity તથા recovery માટે integrated sequence જરૂરી થઈ શકે; દરેક separation માટે distillation જ જરૂરી નથી.

1.6 • Recovery,Fractionation,Batch તથા Steady Operation

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Solute recovery માં desired/unwanted component preferentially દૂર થાય છે. Fractionation માં mixture જુદી compositions ના fractions માં વહેંચાય છે. Unsteady operation માં time સાથે inventory/composition બદલાય છે. Steady operation ના control volume માં time accumulation નથી.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Perfectly mixed batch vessel પણ contact દરમિયાન composition બદલાતી હોવાથી unsteady હોય છે. Continuous plant start-up/upset/shutdown વખતે unsteady હોઈ શકે છે. Steady state પર accumulation નથી, પરંતુ equipment ની length પ્રમાણે composition બદલાઈ શકે છે. Recovery/fractionation separation purpose છે; batch/continuous operation mode છે. આ independent classifications છે, એક જ choice ના alternate names નથી.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

1.7 • Stagewise તથા Continuous-contact Operations

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Stagewise operation માં ઓળખી શકાય તેવા contacting/separation steps હોય છે. Continuous-contact operation માં imposed equilibrium stages વગર contacting region દરમિયાન સતત interfacial exchange થાય છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Ideal stage ના departing phases equilibrium માં હોય છે. Actual stage માટે efficiency જરૂરી છે. Mixer–settlers તથા tray columns stagewise છે. Packed tower differential continuous contact આપે છે અને plant flow steady હોઈ શકે છે. Tray tower માં પણ continuous gas/liquid throughput હોય છે; તેના કારણે contacting differential બનતું નથી. Cascades co-current, countercurrent અથવા crosscurrent હોઈ શકે છે. Arrangement driving force તથા solvent usage બદલે છે.

1. Fundamentals of Mass TransferMass Transfer-I • DI04005021 • Chemical Semester4 • 6h / 12% • GTU2025-26
Syllabus according to detailed theory, derivations, equipment construction and working and worked numericals. Practicals carry official suggested exercises and blank observation sheets — no fabricated results.
1. Notes
1.1 • Mass-transfer operations and their importance

Definition / principle

Mass transfer is the transport of a species relative to a mixture or across a phase boundary under a suitable driving force. A mass-transfer operation uses such transport to separate or recover components.

Detailed theory and conditions

Separation requires both a thermodynamic possibility and a sufficiently rapid rate. Equilibrium limits the attainable separation; diffusion, contact area and contact time influence the rate. Examples include absorbing a gas into a liquid, extracting a solute between two liquids and dissolving soluble material from a solid. A heat exchanger transferring energy is not automatically a mass-transfer separator; pure bulk transport of an unchanged mixture is not selective separation. Material balances establish quantities, while equilibrium and rate information establish achievable compositions and equipment needs.

1.2 • Classification by contacting phases

Definition

Phase-based classification identifies the phases participating in selective component transfer; the operation name also depends on the separating mechanism.

Gas–liquid

Absorption transfers a soluble gas into liquid; stripping transfers a volatile dissolved component from liquid into gas. Distillation uses vapor–liquid equilibrium and energy to redistribute volatile components.

Liquid–liquid

Extraction distributes a solute between two liquid phases that are not completely mutually miscible. The solvent must create a useful selectivity and separable phases.

Solid–liquid and solid–fluid

Leaching dissolves soluble material from a solid using liquid solvent. Adsorption accumulates a component on a solid surface from gas or liquid; it is not bulk absorption. Drying includes transfer of moisture from a wet material to a gas; crystallization forms a solid from a supersaturated liquid.

Qualification

Membrane operations are classified additionally by the selective barrier and driving force; they do not require direct mixing of the two bulk streams. This classification introduces related operations without adding their design derivations to this syllabus.

1.3 • Membrane separation:principle and applications

Definition / principle

Membrane separation uses a selective barrier to preferentially transmit components and retain others; the products are permeate and retentate.

Detailed theory and conditions

A module has a feed side, a selective membrane and a permeate side. Selectivity may arise from pore size or from sorption/diffusion through a dense membrane. Pressure-driven microfiltration/ultrafiltration remove particles or macromolecules; reverse osmosis mainly removes dissolved salts using pressure exceeding the effective osmotic opposition. Gas separation uses permeability/selectivity and a partial-pressure difference; dialysis uses a chemical-potential/concentration driving force, while electrodialysis uses an electric field and ion-selective membranes. Applications include water treatment, protein concentration and gas purification. Fouling, concentration polarization, membrane compatibility, pretreatment, cleaning and energy requirements limit performance. A membrane does not give perfect separation simply because it has small pores.

1.4 • Direct and indirect operations—Treybal classification

Definition / principle

In this classification, direct operations generate the separating phases from the original solution by adding or removing heat. Indirect operations add a foreign separating substance.

Detailed theory and conditions

Classification first: direct examples include fractional distillation and fractional crystallization driven by heat addition/removal. Indirect examples include absorption, stripping, liquid extraction, leaching and adsorption using an added solvent, gas or solid agent. Direct methods avoid a deliberately added separating material, but may require substantial energy. Indirect methods can give a useful selectivity when direct separation is impractical, but solvent/agent recovery, losses, product contamination and materials compatibility can add cost. If the required product is already a solution, the agent need not always be removed. Do not confuse this terminology with physical direct contact: a packed absorber is a direct-contact device but an indirect operation in this textbook classification.[1]

Reference: [1] Treybal, The Mass-Transfer Operations, Chapter1.

1.5 • Choice of separation method

Definition / principle

Choosing a separation method means selecting a feasible operation and separating agent to meet purity, recovery, capacity and safety targets economically.

Detailed theory and conditions

First identify feed phase, composition, flow and target products. Check usable property differences: volatility, solubility, distribution, particle size or membrane permeability. Examine equilibrium selectivity and the obtainable driving force, then rate/contact area and energy or solvent requirements. Include solvent recovery, product contamination, thermal sensitivity, corrosion, toxicity, flammability, waste treatment and control flexibility. A cheap solvent may be expensive overall if it is difficult to regenerate. A single operation may not meet both high recovery and purity, so an integrated sequence may be preferable without assuming that every separation needs distillation.

1.6 • Recovery,fractionation,batch and steady operation

Definition / principle

Solute recovery preferentially removes a desired or unwanted component. Fractionation splits a mixture into fractions of differing compositions. Unsteady operation changes inventory/composition with time; steady operation has no time accumulation in the selected control volume.

Detailed theory and conditions

A batch vessel can be perfectly mixed yet unsteady because solute concentration changes during contact. A continuous plant can be unsteady during start-up, upsets or shutdown. At steady state, inlets and outlets balance without accumulation, although composition can change along the equipment. Solute recovery and fractionation describe separation purpose; batch and continuous describe operation. They are independent classifications rather than mutually exclusive names for the same choice.

Equations and notation

1.7 • Stagewise and continuous-contact operations

Definition / principle

A stagewise operation uses identifiable contacting/separation steps. A continuous-contact operation allows interfacial exchange progressively along the contacting region without imposed equilibrium stages.

Detailed theory and conditions

An ideal stage leaves its exiting phases at equilibrium; an actual stage normally falls short and needs an efficiency definition. Mixer–settlers and tray columns are stagewise contactors. Packed towers provide differential continuous contact, but their plant flow can still be steady. Tray towers may also process continuous gas/liquid flows: continuous throughput does not convert their contacting into differential contact. A cascade connects stages co-currently, countercurrently or crosscurrently; the chosen arrangement changes local driving forces and solvent usage.

Viva questions
1. Define and explain the principle of Mass-transfer operations and their importance.

Mass transfer is the transport of a species relative to a mixture or across a phase boundary under a suitable driving force. A mass-transfer operation uses such transport to separate or recover components. Separation requires both a thermodynamic possibility and a sufficiently rapid rate. Equilibrium limits the attainable separation; diffusion, contact area and contact time influence the rate. Examples include absorbing a gas into a liquid, extracting a solute between two liquids and dissolving soluble material from a solid. A heat exchanger transferring energy is not automatically a mass-transfer separator; pure bulk transport of an unchanged mixture is not selective separation. Material balances establish quantities, while equilibrium and rate information establish achievable compositions and equipment needs.

2. Define and explain the principle of Classification by contacting phases.

Phase-based classification identifies the phases participating in selective component transfer; the operation name also depends on the separating mechanism. Absorption transfers a soluble gas into liquid; stripping transfers a volatile dissolved component from liquid into gas. Distillation uses vapor–liquid equilibrium and energy to redistribute volatile components.

3. Define and explain the principle of Membrane separation:principle and applications.

Membrane separation uses a selective barrier to preferentially transmit components and retain others; the products are permeate and retentate. A module has a feed side, a selective membrane and a permeate side. Selectivity may arise from pore size or from sorption/diffusion through a dense membrane. Pressure-driven microfiltration/ultrafiltration remove particles or macromolecules; reverse osmosis mainly removes dissolved salts using pressure exceeding the effective osmotic opposition. Gas separation uses permeability/selectivity and a partial-pressure difference; dialysis uses a chemical-potential/concentration driving force, while electrodialysis uses an electric field and ion-selective membranes. Applications include water treatment, protein concentration and gas purification. Fouling, concentration polarization, membrane compatibility, pretreatment, cleaning and energy requirements limit performance. A membrane does not give perfect separation simply because it has small pores.

4. Define and explain the principle of Direct and indirect operations—Treybal classification.

In this classification, direct operations generate the separating phases from the original solution by adding or removing heat. Indirect operations add a foreign separating substance. Classification first: direct examples include fractional distillation and fractional crystallization driven by heat addition/removal. Indirect examples include absorption, stripping, liquid extraction, leaching and adsorption using an added solvent, gas or solid agent. Direct methods avoid a deliberately added separating material, but may require substantial energy. Indirect methods can give a useful selectivity when direct separation is impractical, but solvent/agent recovery, losses, product contamination and materials compatibility can add cost. If the required product is already a solution, the agent need not always be removed. Do not confuse this terminology with physical direct contact: a packed absorber is a direct-contact device but an indirect operation in this textbook classification.[1]

5. Define and explain the principle of Choice of separation method.

Choosing a separation method means selecting a feasible operation and separating agent to meet purity, recovery, capacity and safety targets economically. First identify feed phase, composition, flow and target products. Check usable property differences: volatility, solubility, distribution, particle size or membrane permeability. Examine equilibrium selectivity and the obtainable driving force, then rate/contact area and energy or solvent requirements. Include solvent recovery, product contamination, thermal sensitivity, corrosion, toxicity, flammability, waste treatment and control flexibility. A cheap solvent may be expensive overall if it is difficult to regenerate. A single operation may not meet both high recovery and purity, so an integrated sequence may be preferable without assuming that every separation needs distillation.

6. Define and explain the principle of Recovery,fractionation,batch and steady operation.

Solute recovery preferentially removes a desired or unwanted component. Fractionation splits a mixture into fractions of differing compositions. Unsteady operation changes inventory/composition with time; steady operation has no time accumulation in the selected control volume. A batch vessel can be perfectly mixed yet unsteady because solute concentration changes during contact. A continuous plant can be unsteady during start-up, upsets or shutdown. At steady state, inlets and outlets balance without accumulation, although composition can change along the equipment. Solute recovery and fractionation describe separation purpose; batch and continuous describe operation. They are independent classifications rather than mutually exclusive names for the same choice.

7. Define and explain the principle of Stagewise and continuous-contact operations.

A stagewise operation uses identifiable contacting/separation steps. A continuous-contact operation allows interfacial exchange progressively along the contacting region without imposed equilibrium stages. An ideal stage leaves its exiting phases at equilibrium; an actual stage normally falls short and needs an efficiency definition. Mixer–settlers and tray columns are stagewise contactors. Packed towers provide differential continuous contact, but their plant flow can still be steady. Tray towers may also process continuous gas/liquid flows: continuous throughput does not convert their contacting into differential contact. A cascade connects stages co-currently, countercurrently or crosscurrently; the chosen arrangement changes local driving forces and solvent usage.

2. નોટ્સ
2.1 • Molecular તથા Eddy Diffusion

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Random thermal motion તથા composition driving force થી molecular relative transport એટલે molecular diffusion. Turbulent fluid parcels થી વધારાનો transport એટલે eddy diffusion.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Visible mixing વગર પણ gases/liquids માં molecular diffusion થાય છે. Laminar flow માં streamlines વચ્ચે તે કાર્ય કરે છે; laminar bulk flow પોતે eddy diffusion નથી. Turbulent eddies fluid packets ખસેડે છે અને નાના scale પર અંતિમ mixing molecular diffusion થી થાય છે. Molecular diffusivity stated temperature, pressure તથા composition પર mixture property છે. Eddy diffusivity flow, position, direction તથા mixing intensity મુજબ બદલાતું effective parameter છે; બંને interchangeable constants નથી.

2.2 • Rate,Molar Flux,Diffusivity તથા Fick’s Law

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Molar rate એટલે time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles; Molar flux એટલે unit area તથા time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles. Specified reference frame માં composition gradient સાથે diffusive flux જોડતો coefficient diffusivity છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Material balance માટે stationary-coordinate total flux N અને Fick’s law માટે molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J લો. Negative sign composition gradient ની વિરુદ્ધ transport દર્શાવે છે; દરેક numerical flux negative નથી. Gradient spatial derivative છે; distance વગરનો concentration difference નથી. Diffusivity નું dimension area per time છે અને gas values સામાન્ય રીતે liquid કરતાં ઘણી મોટી છે. Total molar concentration c constant હોય ત્યારે concentration derivative વાપરી શકાય; c બદલાય ત્યારે mole-fraction form ને સીધું concentration form ન બનાવો.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

2.3 • Diffusivity પર Temperature,Pressure તથા Composition ની અસર

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Diffusivity transport coefficient છે; તેની value માટે mixture, phase તથા thermodynamic state જણાવવા પડે છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Modest pressure ના dilute gases માં temperature વધતાં diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Fixed temperature પર pressure વધતાં gas diffusivity આશરે inverse રીતે ઘટે છે. Exact exponent correlation-dependent છે; universal power law નથી. Temperature વધતાં viscosity ઘટે તેથી liquid diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Ordinary pressure ની liquid પર અસર gas કરતાં ઓછી છે. Composition થી viscosity, interactions તથા mutual diffusivity બદલાય છે, ખાસ કરીને concentrated liquids માં. Range દરમિયાન D ઘણું બદલાય તો એક average D વડે integration approximation છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

2.4 • Derivation:Binary Mutual Diffusivity DAB = DBA

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Binary mixture, same local state તથા molar-mean reference frame લો. Mutual diffusivities માટે derivation છે; અલગ self-diffusion coefficients માટે નહીં. c total molar concentration અને y mole fraction છે.

  1. Binary composition condition.

  2. આ reference frame માં diffusive flux નો સરવાળો zero છે.

  3. બંને species માટે Fick’s law લો.

  4. Binary gradient relation મૂકો.

  5. Nonzero composition gradient માટે mutual coefficients સમાન છે. Zero-gradient condition થી numerical D શોધી શકાતું નથી.

2.5 • Derivation:General Molar-flux Equation

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

z direction માં one-dimensional transport લો. vA, vB species velocities અને v* molar-mean velocity છે. Binary Fickian diffusion લો. Simple integration માટે આગળ c, D constant માનવામાં આવશે.

  1. Total species flux તથા molar-mean velocity.

  2. Relative તથા bulk motion અલગ કરો.

  3. Fick’s mole-fraction form મૂકો.

  4. Steady, nonreacting, constant-area layer માં species flux constant છે.

  5. Mixture molar rest માટે NT=0 છે; stagnant component માટે NB=0 છે. બીજા case માં Stefan bulk flow હોઈ શકે છે. Laminar flow માં પણ bulk velocity nonzero હોઈ શકે છે.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady one-dimensional binary ideal gas; reaction નહીં. T, P, ideal-gas concentration c, D તથા area constant. L=z2−z1 તથા NB=0. yA1>yA2 હોય તો direction2 તરફ positive flux છે. R તથા molar units consistent રાખો.

  1. General equation માં NB=0 મૂકો.

  2. Variables separate કરીને layer ઉપર integrate કરો.

  3. Limits મૂકો.

  4. pA=PyA તથા ideal-gas concentration લો.

  5. B partial pressures નો logarithmic mean લો. Equal endpoints માટે continuous limit લો.

  6. Equivalent form માં P/pBM factor Stefan flow દર્શાવે છે.

2.7 • Derivation:Gases માં Equimolar Counterdiffusion

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady ideal-gas, T, P, D તથા area constant લો. NA=−NB હોવાથી molar bulk flux zero છે. આ stagnant B condition નથી.

  1. Equal તથા opposite species fluxes લો.

  2. General equation નો bulk term zero કરો.

  3. Flux, c તથા D constant રાખીને integrate કરો.

  4. Limits મૂકી partial pressures માં ફેરવો.

  5. B નું magnitude સમાન અને direction વિરુદ્ધ છે.

2.8 • Derivation:Liquid A through Non-diffusing B

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady binary liquid, D તથા આશરે total molar concentration c constant, NB=0, no reaction તથા plane layer L લો. x liquid mole fraction અને cA=cxA છે. Mole fraction ને conversion વગર mass fraction ન માનો.

  1. General equation માં liquid mole fraction લો.

  2. Separate કરીને integrate કરો.

  3. Finite-concentration result મેળવો.

  4. B નો log-mean mole fraction લો.

  5. Concentration form લખો. A sufficiently dilute હોય તો xBM આશરે 1 થાય છે.

Steady binary liquid, equal opposite molar fluxes, આશરે constant c, D તથા plane layer, no reaction લો. Molar masses જુદા હોય તો equal molar flux એટલે equal mass flux નથી.

Liquid-system Diffusivity—Room Temperature

હેતુ તથા Official Scope

Approved cell/method વડે liquid mutual diffusivity શોધો. Calibrated diaphragm-cell method એક suitable format છે; GTU-prescribed apparatus claim નથી.

Apparatus તથા તૈયારી

બે well-mixed compartments, validated cell constant, T control, timer તથા approved dilute electrolyte માટે conductivity જેવી calibrated assay લો.

Principle તથા Assumptions

Constant-D calibrated-cell model માં concentration difference આશરે exponentially ઘટે છે. Kcell માં geometry/porosity corrections છે તથા units m⁻² છે; unverified pore-size guess નહીં.

Procedure તથા Record

Approved initial concentrations લો, bubbles વગર fill કરો તથા diaphragm માં bulk leakage ન થાય તેવું prescribed mixing રાખો. Validated calibration થી બંને compartment concentrations સામે time નોંધો. Sampling/replacement correction કરો. Actual room temperature તથા log concentration-difference/time fit આપો.

વાઇવા પ્રશ્નો
1. Molecular તથા Eddy Diffusion ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Random thermal motion તથા composition driving force થી molecular relative transport એટલે molecular diffusion. Turbulent fluid parcels થી વધારાનો transport એટલે eddy diffusion. Visible mixing વગર પણ gases/liquids માં molecular diffusion થાય છે. Laminar flow માં streamlines વચ્ચે તે કાર્ય કરે છે; laminar bulk flow પોતે eddy diffusion નથી. Turbulent eddies fluid packets ખસેડે છે અને નાના scale પર અંતિમ mixing molecular diffusion થી થાય છે. Molecular diffusivity stated temperature, pressure તથા composition પર mixture property છે. Eddy diffusivity flow, position, direction તથા mixing intensity મુજબ બદલાતું effective parameter છે; બંને interchangeable constants નથી.

2. Rate,Molar Flux,Diffusivity તથા Fick’s Law ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Molar rate એટલે time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles; Molar flux એટલે unit area તથા time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles. Specified reference frame માં composition gradient સાથે diffusive flux જોડતો coefficient diffusivity છે. Material balance માટે stationary-coordinate total flux N અને Fick’s law માટે molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J લો. Negative sign composition gradient ની વિરુદ્ધ transport દર્શાવે છે; દરેક numerical flux negative નથી. Gradient spatial derivative છે; distance વગરનો concentration difference નથી. Diffusivity નું dimension area per time છે અને gas values સામાન્ય રીતે liquid કરતાં ઘણી મોટી છે. Total molar concentration c constant હોય ત્યારે concentration derivative વાપરી શકાય; c બદલાય ત્યારે mole-fraction form ને સીધું concentration form ન બનાવો.

3. Diffusivity પર Temperature,Pressure તથા Composition ની અસર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Diffusivity transport coefficient છે; તેની value માટે mixture, phase તથા thermodynamic state જણાવવા પડે છે. Modest pressure ના dilute gases માં temperature વધતાં diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Fixed temperature પર pressure વધતાં gas diffusivity આશરે inverse રીતે ઘટે છે. Exact exponent correlation-dependent છે; universal power law નથી. Temperature વધતાં viscosity ઘટે તેથી liquid diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Ordinary pressure ની liquid પર અસર gas કરતાં ઓછી છે. Composition થી viscosity, interactions તથા mutual diffusivity બદલાય છે, ખાસ કરીને concentrated liquids માં. Range દરમિયાન D ઘણું બદલાય તો એક average D વડે integration approximation છે.

2. Molecular Diffusion in FluidsMass Transfer-I • DI04005021 • Chemical Semester4 • 9h / 20% • GTU2025-26
Syllabus according to detailed theory, derivations, equipment construction and working and worked numericals. Practicals carry official suggested exercises and blank observation sheets — no fabricated results.
2. Notes
2.1 • Molecular and eddy diffusion

Definition / principle

Molecular diffusion is relative molecular transport caused by random thermal motion and a composition driving force. Eddy diffusion is additional transport by turbulent fluid parcels.

Detailed theory and conditions

Molecular diffusion occurs in gases and liquids even without visible mixing. In laminar flow it acts across streamlines; laminar bulk flow itself is not eddy diffusion. Turbulent eddies transport packets of fluid, but molecular diffusion finally mixes at small scales. Molecular diffusivity is a mixture property at stated temperature, pressure and composition; eddy diffusivity is an effective flow-dependent parameter and can vary with position, direction and mixing intensity. They are not interchangeable constants.

2.2 • Rate,molar flux,diffusivity and Fick’s law

Definition / principle

Molar rate is amount transferred per time. Molar flux is amount crossing unit area per time. Diffusivity relates diffusive flux to the composition gradient in a specified reference frame.

Detailed theory and conditions

Use total stationary-coordinate flux N for material balances and molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J in Fick’s law. The negative sign means diffusion down the composition gradient, not that every reported flux is negative. The gradient is a spatial derivative, not a concentration difference without division by distance. Diffusivity has dimensions area per time; gas values are usually much larger than liquid values. For constant total molar concentration c, Fick’s law may also use the concentration derivative. If c varies, the mole-fraction form must not be casually replaced by the concentration form.

Equations and notation

2.3 • Effect of temperature,pressure and composition on diffusivity

Definition / principle

Diffusivity is a transport coefficient whose numerical value requires a specified mixture, phase and thermodynamic state.

Detailed theory and conditions

For dilute gases at modest pressure, increasing temperature increases molecular motion and generally increases diffusivity; at fixed temperature increasing pressure usually decreases gas diffusivity approximately inversely. Gas correlations and their exponent are model-dependent, not a universal exact power law. Liquid diffusivity generally rises with temperature as viscosity decreases; its ordinary-pressure dependence is weaker than that of gases. Composition can change viscosity, interactions and mutual diffusivity, especially in concentrated liquids. A single average D in an integrated equation is an approximation if D varies strongly over the composition range.

Equations and notation

2.4 • Derivation:binary mutual diffusivity DAB = DBA

Symbols, model and assumptions

Binary mixture; the same local state and molar-mean reference frame. Use mutual diffusivities, not unrelated self-diffusion coefficients. c is total molar concentration and y is mole fraction.

  1. Binary composition constraint.

  2. Diffusive fluxes sum to zero in this frame.

  3. Apply Fick’s law to both species.

  4. Substitute the binary gradient relation.

  5. For a nonzero composition gradient, the mutual coefficients are equal. The zero-gradient case cannot determine a numerical D.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: binary constraint → zero sum of J → substitute Fick’s laws → equality. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

2.5 • Derivation:general molar-flux equation

Symbols, model and assumptions

One-dimensional transport along z; vA, vB are species molar velocities and v* is molar-mean velocity. Fickian binary diffusion is assumed. D and c need be constant only for subsequent simple integration.

  1. Define total species fluxes and molar-mean velocity.

  2. Separate relative motion from bulk motion.

  3. Insert the mole-fraction form of Fick’s law.

  4. For a steady, nonreacting constant-area layer, the species flux is constant.

  5. A mixture at molar rest has NT=0. A stagnant component means NB=0 instead; bulk Stefan flow may then exist. Laminar flow can still have nonzero bulk velocity.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: define v* and J → rearrange → substitute Fick’s law → specify which flux constraint applies. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

2.6 • Derivation:gas A through stagnant non-diffusing B

Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady, one-dimensional binary ideal gas; no reaction; constant T, P, ideal-gas concentration c, D and area; layer thickness L=z2−z1; NB=0. yA1>yA2 gives positive flux toward2. R must match the molar units used.

  1. Insert NB=0 into the general equation.

  2. Separate and integrate across the layer.

  3. Evaluate limits.

  4. Use pA=PyA and ideal-gas concentration.

  5. Define the logarithmic mean of the B partial pressures; use its continuous equal-endpoint limit if necessary.

  6. Equivalent form; the factor P/pBM accounts for Stefan flow.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: NB=0 → separation/integral → logarithmic flux with assumptions. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

2.7 • Derivation:equimolar counterdiffusion in gases

Symbols, model and assumptions

Same steady ideal-gas, constant T, P, D and area assumptions; NA=−NB, so molar bulk flux is zero. This is not the same condition as stagnant B.

  1. Impose equal and opposite species fluxes.

  2. Remove the bulk term from the general equation.

  3. Integrate with constant flux, c and D.

  4. Evaluate and convert to partial pressures.

  5. B has equal magnitude and reverse direction.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: NT=0 → Fick form → integral → partial-pressure result. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

2.8 • Derivation:liquid A through non-diffusing B

Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady binary liquid; constant D and approximately constant total molar concentration c; NB=0; no reaction; plane layer L. x is liquid mole fraction, cA=cxA. Do not replace mole fraction by mass fraction without conversion.

  1. Use the liquid mole fraction in the general equation.

  2. Separate and integrate.

  3. Obtain the finite-concentration result.

  4. Introduce the log-mean mole fraction of B.

  5. Write concentration form. For a sufficiently dilute A, xBM approaches1.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: NB=0 → integrate mole fraction → logarithmic flux; state constant-c approximation. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

2.9 • Derivation:equimolar counterdiffusion in liquids

Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady binary liquid; equal opposite molar fluxes; approximately constant c and D; plane layer; no reaction. This idealization need not imply equal and opposite mass fluxes if molar masses differ.

  1. Specify zero net molar bulk flux.

  2. Apply the relative-flux law.

  3. Integrate with stated constant properties.

  4. Express in mole fractions or molar concentrations.

  5. State the companion species flux.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: NT=0 → Fick law → integrated concentration difference with units. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

Solved numericals and practicals
Gas–liquid-system diffusivity at room temperature

Objective and official scope

Determine the relevant diffusivity using the institution-approved gas–liquid apparatus. The common Stefan evaporation method below determines vapor A in carrier gas B above a liquid, not dissolved-gas diffusivity inside the liquid.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved diffusion cell, bath, temperature/pressure measurement, level microscope, timer and validated liquid density/vapor-pressure data. Use the actual apparatus manual if it employs a different method.

Principle and assumptions

For a quasi-steady gas film with NB=0, interface saturation and a controlled upper boundary, level retreat gives a z²-versus-time slope.ρL is liquid density, MA is kg per mole, all gas units are consistent.

Procedure and record

Under supervision establish a constant bath state, measure total pressure and reference level, then record elapsed time and diffusion length without inventing readings. Fit z² versus time and use the boundary vapor fractions appropriate to the actual rig. Report the measured room temperature rather than assuming25°C.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Only approved volatile liquids and rated apparatus; ventilation, no ignition source, and no improvised heating or gas pressurization. Check leaks, bath stability, boundary control and whether the quasi-steady model applies.

Liquid-system diffusivity at room temperature

Objective and official scope

Determine liquid-phase mutual diffusivity using the approved cell/method. A calibrated diaphragm-cell method is described as one suitable format, not as a prescribed GTU apparatus.

Apparatus and preparation

Two well-mixed liquid compartments, validated diaphragm-cell constant, temperature control, timer and calibrated composition assay such as conductivity for an approved dilute electrolyte.

Principle and assumptions

A concentration difference decays approximately exponentially under a constant-D calibrated-cell model. Kcell includes geometry/porosity corrections and has units m⁻²; it is not an unverified pore-size guess.

Procedure and record

Prepare approved initial concentrations, fill without bubbles and maintain prescribed mixing without driving bulk leakage through the diaphragm. Record concentration in both compartments versus time using the validated calibration. Correct for sample withdrawal or replacement. Report actual room temperature and fit log concentration difference against time.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Follow the cell-specific procedure; some rigs require another relation. Stirrer heat, temperature-sensitive conductivity, unmixed boundary layers and leakage bias D. No fabricated cell constant or measurements.

Viva questions
1. Define and explain the principle of Molecular and eddy diffusion.

Molecular diffusion is relative molecular transport caused by random thermal motion and a composition driving force. Eddy diffusion is additional transport by turbulent fluid parcels. Molecular diffusion occurs in gases and liquids even without visible mixing. In laminar flow it acts across streamlines; laminar bulk flow itself is not eddy diffusion. Turbulent eddies transport packets of fluid, but molecular diffusion finally mixes at small scales. Molecular diffusivity is a mixture property at stated temperature, pressure and composition; eddy diffusivity is an effective flow-dependent parameter and can vary with position, direction and mixing intensity. They are not interchangeable constants.

2. Define and explain the principle of Rate,molar flux,diffusivity and Fick’s law.

Molar rate is amount transferred per time. Molar flux is amount crossing unit area per time. Diffusivity relates diffusive flux to the composition gradient in a specified reference frame. Use total stationary-coordinate flux N for material balances and molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J in Fick’s law. The negative sign means diffusion down the composition gradient, not that every reported flux is negative. The gradient is a spatial derivative, not a concentration difference without division by distance. Diffusivity has dimensions area per time; gas values are usually much larger than liquid values. For constant total molar concentration c, Fick’s law may also use the concentration derivative. If c varies, the mole-fraction form must not be casually replaced by the concentration form.

3. Define and explain the principle of Effect of temperature,pressure and composition on diffusivity.

Diffusivity is a transport coefficient whose numerical value requires a specified mixture, phase and thermodynamic state. For dilute gases at modest pressure, increasing temperature increases molecular motion and generally increases diffusivity; at fixed temperature increasing pressure usually decreases gas diffusivity approximately inversely. Gas correlations and their exponent are model-dependent, not a universal exact power law. Liquid diffusivity generally rises with temperature as viscosity decreases; its ordinary-pressure dependence is weaker than that of gases. Composition can change viscosity, interactions and mutual diffusivity, especially in concentrated liquids. A single average D in an integrated equation is an approximation if D varies strongly over the composition range.

3. નોટ્સ
3.1 • Phase Equilibrium તથા Driving Force

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified state પર contacting phases વચ્ચે species ની net transfer tendency ન હોય તે phase equilibrium છે. Interface ની બંને બાજુ chemical potentials સમાન હોય છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Equilibrium માં gas/liquid concentrations સમાન હોવી જરૂરી નથી. y*=mx જેવી relation liquid composition સાથે equilibrium gas composition જોડે છે. Asterisk corresponding equilibrium value છે, measured bulk value નહીં. Absorption માટે ybulk>y*(xbulk) હોય તો gas-to-liquid tendency છે. Plot પર T, P, species તથા composition basis લખો; તે બદલાય તો equilibrium relation બદલાય છે. Two-film model માં local interface equilibrium assumption છે; સમગ્ર equipment equilibrium માં નથી. Bulk phases equilibrium relation satisfy કરે ત્યારે net driving force zero થાય છે છતાં molecular motion ચાલુ રહે છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

3.2 • Two-film Concept તથા Local/Overall Coefficients

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Two-film model માં interface ની બંને બાજુ gas તથા liquid films થી resistances દર્શાવાય છે. Local coefficient bulk-to-interface driving force અને overall coefficient equivalent bulk-to-bulk driving force વાપરે છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Gas solute gas film માંથી interface સુધી અને પછી liquid film માંથી bulk માં જાય છે. Interface equilibrium માનવામાં આવે છે. Steady condition માં બંને film ના flux સમાન છે, compositions નહીં. Mole-fraction convention માં ky, kx ના units flux per mole fraction છે. Pressure-based KG તથા concentration-based kL ના dimensions જુદા છે; equilibrium conversion વગર reciprocals ન ઉમેરો. Overall coefficients અજાણ interface compositions ટાળે છે, પરંતુ બંને resistances તથા equilibrium slope પર આધારિત છે. Nonlinear relation માટે યોગ્ય local slope/segment લો; સમગ્ર column માટે arbitrary m ન મૂકો.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Gas માંથી liquid માં A નો steady transfer; interface accumulation/reaction નહીં. yi=mxi તથા positive constant m લો. બધાં coefficients માટે same molar-flux/mole-fraction basis રાખો.

3.4 • Coefficients ના Uses તથા Controlling Resistance

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Consistent driving-force basis પર overall resistance માં જે film contribution સૌથી મોટું હોય તે controlling resistance છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Gas basis પર 1/ky તથા m/kx સરખાવો; ફક્ત ky, kx નહીં. Gas resistance dominant હોય તો gas-side mixing/area સુધારવું વધુ ઉપયોગી છે. Liquid resistance dominant હોય તો liquid mixing/interface renewal મદદ કરે છે. Small equilibrium slope gas-side control ને favor કરી શકે; large m liquid resistance વધારી શકે, પરંતુ actual terms સરખાવવા પડે. Local coefficients correlations/film effects માટે અને overall coefficients accessible bulk samples થી rate/design માટે ઉપયોગી છે. Coefficient અથવા equilibrium data એકલાં total transfer આપતાં નથી; area તથા compatible driving force જોઈએ.

3.5 • Ideal Stage,Stage Efficiency તથા Cascade Types

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Departing phases ને equilibrium સુધી લાવતો stage ideal equilibrium stage છે. Actual stage finite contact થી તે limit સુધી આંશિક પહોંચે છે. Interconnected contacting stages ની series cascade છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Same duty માટે theoretical stages ને actual stages થી ભાગો તે overall tray efficiency છે. Murphree gas efficiency actual gas-composition change ને tray છોડી રહેલા liquid સાથે equilibrium ideal change સામે સરખાવે છે; તે total solute recovery નથી. Countercurrent માં phases opposite જાય છે તથા solvent demand ઘણી વખત ઓછી રહે છે. Co-current માં same direction માં જઈ common equilibrium limit તરફ પહોંચે છે. Crosscurrent extraction માં successive raffinate ને fresh solvent portions મળે છે અને extracts અલગ નીકળે છે. કઈ efficiency તથા composition basis છે તે સ્પષ્ટ કરો.

3. Interphase Mass TransferMass Transfer-I • DI04005021 • Chemical Semester4 • 4h / 10% • GTU2025-26
Syllabus according to detailed theory, derivations, equipment construction and working and worked numericals. Practicals carry official suggested exercises and blank observation sheets — no fabricated results.
3. Notes
3.1 • Phase equilibrium and driving force

Definition / principle

Phase equilibrium is a state with no net transfer tendency for a species between contacting phases at the specified state; its chemical potentials are equal across the interface.

Detailed theory and conditions

Equilibrium does not require equal concentrations in gas and liquid. A relation such as y*=mx connects the gas composition in equilibrium with a liquid composition; the asterisk means the corresponding equilibrium value, not a measured bulk value. For absorption, ybulk exceeding y*(xbulk) gives a gas-to-liquid tendency. A plot must identify temperature, pressure, composition basis and species; changing these changes the equilibrium relation. Local interface equilibrium is a two-film model assumption and need not mean the entire equipment is at equilibrium. If the bulk phases already match their equilibrium relation, the driving force vanishes even though molecules still move in both directions.

Equations and notation

3.2 • Two-film concept and local versus overall coefficients

Definition / principle

The two-film model represents resistance on both sides of an interface by gas-side and liquid-side films. A local coefficient uses bulk-to-interface driving force; an overall coefficient uses an equivalent bulk-to-bulk driving force.

Detailed theory and conditions

A gas solute diffuses through the gas film, passes an interface assumed at equilibrium and diffuses into the liquid bulk. At steady interfacial transfer without accumulation, the flux through both films is equal, not the compositions. In the mole-fraction convention, ky and kx have units molar flux per mole fraction. KG based on pressure and kL based on liquid molar concentration have different dimensions; never add their reciprocal resistances without the appropriate equilibrium conversion. Overall coefficients avoid the usually unmeasured interface compositions but still depend on both film resistances and the equilibrium slope. For nonlinear equilibrium use a suitable local slope/segment and do not insert one arbitrary constant m across the whole column.

Equations and notation

3.3 • Derivation:overall two-phase mass-transfer resistances

Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady transfer A from gas to liquid; no interfacial accumulation/reaction; linear local equilibrium yi=mxi with constant positive m; same molar-flux and mole-fraction bases throughout.

  1. Write gas-side and liquid-side drops.

  2. Split the gas-based overall driving force.

  3. Use interface and conjugate bulk equilibrium.

  4. Substitute film drops.

  5. Compare with the overall gas-side definition.

  6. For the liquid basis, split x*−x and divide the gas drop by m.

  7. The liquid overall result and conversion follow.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: write film fluxes → split gas driving force → convert liquid drop by m → reciprocal resistance result. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

3.4 • Uses and controlling resistance

Definition / principle

The controlling resistance is the film contribution dominating the overall resistance on a consistently chosen driving-force basis.

Detailed theory and conditions

On the gas basis compare1/ky with m/kx, not ky and kx alone. If the gas contribution dominates, increasing gas-side mixing/area is more helpful than improving an already negligible liquid resistance. If the liquid contribution dominates, liquid mixing and interfacial renewal may help. A small equilibrium slope generally favors gas-side control; large m may emphasize liquid-side resistance, but actual coefficients must still be compared. Local coefficients are useful for correlations and identifying film effects; overall coefficients are convenient in design/rate measurements using accessible bulk samples. Neither a larger coefficient nor equilibrium data alone specifies the total transfer without area and a compatible driving force.

3.5 • Ideal stage,stage efficiency and cascade types

Definition / principle

An ideal equilibrium stage brings the departing phases to equilibrium. An actual stage provides finite contact and may approach that limit only partly. A cascade is an interconnected series of contacting stages.

Detailed theory and conditions

Overall tray efficiency is the number of theoretical stages divided by the actual stages for the same duty. Murphree gas efficiency compares the actual gas-composition change with the ideal change relative to liquid leaving that tray; it is not the same as total solute recovery. Countercurrent cascades send phases oppositely and commonly maintain useful driving forces with lower solvent demand. Co-current cascades send both phases in the same direction and approach a common equilibrium limit. Crosscurrent extraction contacts successive raffinate streams with fresh solvent portions; the solvent extracts leave separately unless combined downstream. Always state which efficiency and composition basis are being used.

Equations and notation

Viva questions
1. Define and explain the principle of Phase equilibrium and driving force.

Phase equilibrium is a state with no net transfer tendency for a species between contacting phases at the specified state; its chemical potentials are equal across the interface. Equilibrium does not require equal concentrations in gas and liquid. A relation such as y*=mx connects the gas composition in equilibrium with a liquid composition; the asterisk means the corresponding equilibrium value, not a measured bulk value. For absorption, ybulk exceeding y*(xbulk) gives a gas-to-liquid tendency. A plot must identify temperature, pressure, composition basis and species; changing these changes the equilibrium relation. Local interface equilibrium is a two-film model assumption and need not mean the entire equipment is at equilibrium. If the bulk phases already match their equilibrium relation, the driving force vanishes even though molecules still move in both directions.

2. Define and explain the principle of Two-film concept and local versus overall coefficients.

The two-film model represents resistance on both sides of an interface by gas-side and liquid-side films. A local coefficient uses bulk-to-interface driving force; an overall coefficient uses an equivalent bulk-to-bulk driving force. A gas solute diffuses through the gas film, passes an interface assumed at equilibrium and diffuses into the liquid bulk. At steady interfacial transfer without accumulation, the flux through both films is equal, not the compositions. In the mole-fraction convention, ky and kx have units molar flux per mole fraction. KG based on pressure and kL based on liquid molar concentration have different dimensions; never add their reciprocal resistances without the appropriate equilibrium conversion. Overall coefficients avoid the usually unmeasured interface compositions but still depend on both film resistances and the equilibrium slope. For nonlinear equilibrium use a suitable local slope/segment and do not insert one arbitrary constant m across the whole column.

3. Define and explain the principle of Uses and controlling resistance.

The controlling resistance is the film contribution dominating the overall resistance on a consistently chosen driving-force basis. On the gas basis compare1/ky with m/kx, not ky and kx alone. If the gas contribution dominates, increasing gas-side mixing/area is more helpful than improving an already negligible liquid resistance. If the liquid contribution dominates, liquid mixing and interfacial renewal may help. A small equilibrium slope generally favors gas-side control; large m may emphasize liquid-side resistance, but actual coefficients must still be compared. Local coefficients are useful for correlations and identifying film effects; overall coefficients are convenient in design/rate measurements using accessible bulk samples. Neither a larger coefficient nor equilibrium data alone specifies the total transfer without area and a compatible driving force.

4. Define and explain the principle of Ideal stage,stage efficiency and cascade types.

An ideal equilibrium stage brings the departing phases to equilibrium. An actual stage provides finite contact and may approach that limit only partly. A cascade is an interconnected series of contacting stages. Overall tray efficiency is the number of theoretical stages divided by the actual stages for the same duty. Murphree gas efficiency compares the actual gas-composition change with the ideal change relative to liquid leaving that tray; it is not the same as total solute recovery. Countercurrent cascades send phases oppositely and commonly maintain useful driving forces with lower solvent demand. Co-current cascades send both phases in the same direction and approach a common equilibrium limit. Crosscurrent extraction contacts successive raffinate streams with fresh solvent portions; the solvent extracts leave separately unless combined downstream. Always state which efficiency and composition basis are being used.

4. Gas AbsorptionMass Transfer-I • DI04005021 • Chemical Semester4 • 8h / 18% • GTU2025-26
Syllabus મુજબ વિગતવાર Theory, derivations, equipment ના Construction/Working તથા worked Numericals. Practical માં official suggested exercises તથા blank observation sheets છે—fabricated results નથી.
4. નોટ્સ
4.1 • Gas Absorption ના પ્રકાર

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Gas mixture ના એક અથવા વધુ components ને contacting liquid solvent માં transfer કરવું એટલે gas absorption. Desorption/stripping તેની reverse transfer છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Classification: physical absorption માં intended chemical reaction વગર gas dissolve થાય છે. Chemical absorption માં dissolution સાથે liquid reaction જોડાય છે. Single/multicomponent તથા batch/continuous independent classifications છે. Reaction driving force જાળવી શકે છે, પરંતુ reagent, heat, regeneration તથા reaction-equilibrium requirements ઉમેરે છે. Liquid bulk absorption ને solid-surface adsorption સાથે ન ભેળવો.

4.2 • Absorption ના Industrial Applications

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Industrial absorption duty માં recover/remove કરવો તે gas solute, solvent તથા treated-gas/liquid-product quality નક્કી થાય છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Ammonia ને water માં recover કરવું, suitable reactive solvent થી acid-gas treatment તથા process/off-gas ના soluble contaminants દૂર કરવાં examples છે. Solvent actual chemistry મુજબ જોઈએ; water universal solvent નથી. Reactive scrubber તથા physical solvent ના waste/regeneration loads જુદા છે. Absorber saleable solution, valuable-species recovery, downstream protection અથવા emission control માટે હોઈ શકે છે. Feed variation, heat release, mist, corrosion તથા solvent handling ફક્ત material balance થી solve થતા નથી.

4.3 • Gas Solubility,Equilibrium તથા T/P ની અસર

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified temperature, gas partial pressure તથા liquid composition પર equilibrium dissolved amount એટલે gas solubility. Henry’s law stated convention ધરાવતી dilute-solution equilibrium relation છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Pressure-per-mole-fraction convention માં pA=HA xA એટલે yA*=HA xA/P લો. Fixed temperature પર solute partial pressure વધતાં physical solubility સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Gas mole fraction fixed રાખીને total pressure વધારવાથી partial pressure વધે છે; solute partial pressure fixed હોય તો સમાન solubility increase નહીં મળે. ઘણા physical systems માં dissolution exothermic હોવાથી temperature વધતાં solubility ઘટે છે, પરંતુ actual equilibrium data તપાસો. Reaction થી trend બદલાઈ શકે છે. Nonlinear/concentrated/reactive system માટે એક Henry constant સમગ્ર range માં valid ન હોઈ શકે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

4.4 • Ideal Liquid Solution તથા Raoult’s Law

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Raoult standard-state basis પર activity coefficients unit હોય તે ideal liquid solution છે. Volatile liquid component ના equilibrium partial pressure ને liquid mole fraction તથા pure-component saturation pressure સાથે Raoult’s law જોડે છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Fixed temperature પર ideal liquid તથા approximately ideal vapor માટે pA*=xA pA, sat છે. Saturation pressure temperature પર ખૂબ આધારિત છે. Equilibrium gas fraction pA*/P છે. દરેક sparingly soluble/reacting gas માટે આ universal law નથી; dilute solute માટે Henry standard state વધુ યોગ્ય હોઈ શકે છે. Ideal mixing એટલે બંને phases ની compositions સમાન નહીં. Ideal assumptions fail થાય તો activity/fugacity corrections જોઈએ.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

4.5 • Absorption Solvent ની પસંદગી

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

પૂરતી selective capacity સાથે circulation, separation, regeneration તથા safe handling માટે practical હોય તે suitable absorption solvent છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Target-gas solubility/selectivity, low volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability તથા low corrosion જુઓ. Toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost તથા material compatibility સામેલ કરો. Regeneration energy તથા loaded-solvent treatment/disposal ગણો. Low volatility solvent loss ઘટાડે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping ને મદદ કરે છે પણ poor selectivity સુધારતી નથી. Reactive solvent માં heat removal તથા regeneration/reagent replacement જોઈએ. ફક્ત સૌથી ઊંચી equilibrium loading પરથી solvent ન પસંદ કરો.

4.6 • Solute-free Material-balance Basis

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Solute-free flow એટલે nontransferring carrier gas અથવા solvent નો flow. Y તથા X અનુક્રમે carrier-gas mole તથા solvent mole દીઠ solute moles છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

એક-component transfer અને negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution તથા reaction માટે Vs, Ls constant રહે છે, જ્યારે total flows બદલાઈ શકે છે. Displayed solute-free conversion ratios dilute approximation સિવાય mole fractions સમાન નથી. બધા streams માટે same molar/time basis લો અને endpoints entering/exiting પ્રમાણે label કરો. Henry નું linear y*=mx exact solute-free X, Y માં linear નથી; converted relation અથવા સ્પષ્ટ dilute approximation લો.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

4.7 • Derivation:Countercurrent Absorber Material Balance

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, એક transferred solute, constant carrier flows Vs, Ls તથા negligible solvent volatility/inert dissolution લો. X, Y solute-free molar ratios છે.

  1. Gas rich→lean તથા liquid lean→rich માટે overall solute balance.

  2. Transferred amount પ્રમાણે rearrange કરો.

  3. Top થી local section સુધી balance લો. Top gas Yout તથા liquid Xin છે.

  4. Positive-slope operating line મેળવો. Endpoints (Xin, Yout) તથા (Xout, Yin) છે.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

4.8 • Derivation:Co-current Absorber Material Balance

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, એક transferred solute, constant carrier flows Vs, Ls તથા negligible solvent volatility/inert dissolution લો. X, Y solute-free molar ratios છે.

  1. બંને streams same end પર Yin તથા Xin સાથે enter થાય છે.

  2. કોઈ પણ common position માટે rearrange કરો.

  3. આ X, Y plot પર local operating-line slope negative છે.

  4. Common outlet પર overall balance form સમાન છે, પરંતુ endpoint pairing તથા attainable approach જુદાં છે.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

4.9 • Derivation:Minimum Liquid-to-gas Ratio

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Constant-carrier countercurrent model તથા specified Yin, Yout, Xin અને equilibrium curve લો. Bottom pinch formula ત્યારે જ લો જ્યારે તે controlling હોય. Interior tangency તથા સમગ્ર range તપાસો.

  1. Overall transfer balance લો.

  2. Bottom-controlled pinch માટે minimum solvent એટલે સૌથી મોટી thermodynamically admissible outlet loading.

  3. Limiting loading મૂકો.

  4. આપેલું equilibrium model solute-free ratios માં linear હોય ત્યારે જ Xout, max આ રીતે લો.

  5. Minimum પર pinch ની local driving force zero થાય છે અને ideal finite-rate model માં required size અનંત તરફ જાય છે. Actual ratio feasible minimum કરતાં વધુ લો.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

4.10 • HETP તથા તેનો યોગ્ય ઉપયોગ

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified conditions પર એક theoretical equilibrium stage જેટલું separation આપતી active packed height એટલે Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate, HETP.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

N theoretical stages જેટલા separation માટે active packed height Z=N×HETP છે. HETP physical tray spacing નથી તથા packing ની એકલ universal property નથી. Mixture, loading, wetting, distribution તથા conditions પર આધારિત છે. Distributors, demisters તથા disengagement માટે વધારાની જગ્યા હોવાથી total vessel height active packing કરતાં વધુ હોય છે. HETP ને height of transfer unit સાથે ન ભેળવો; અહીં syllabus મુજબ HETP છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

4.11 • Tray Tower Absorber

વ્યાખ્યા

Rising gas ને flowing liquid માં વારંવાર disperse કરવા trays ધરાવતો vertical gas–liquid contactor છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

દરેક tray પર interfacial contact થી soluble gas liquid તરફ transfer થાય છે. Successive trays stagewise countercurrent cascade બનાવે છે.

રચના (Construction)

Vertical shell માં horizontal trays, gas passages, liquid weirs તથા downcomers છે. Drawing sieve-tray arrangement બતાવે છે; valve તથા bubble-cap alternatives છે. Gas નીચે enter થાય છે અને lean solvent upper tray ઉપરથી આવે છે. Treated gas top mist eliminator તરફથી તથા rich liquid bottom sump માંથી નીકળે છે. Downcomer outlet liquid seal જાળવે છે. Supports/access inspection માટે છે. Trays distinct contacting levels આપે છે, continuous packed surface નહીં.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Gas openings માંથી ઊઠીને retained liquid માં bubbles બનાવે છે. Liquid tray ઉપરથી weir પાર કરીને downcomer વડે lower tray પર જાય છે. Interface પરથી solute transfer થતાં ઉપર જતો gas lean અને નીચે જતું liquid rich બને છે. Low gas થી weeping તથા excessive loading થી entrainment/flooding થઈ શકે છે. Actual departures equilibrium સુધી પહોંચે જ એવું નથી. બંને feeds continuous છે પણ contacting stagewise છે; syllabus નું continuous-equipment grouping throughput માટે છે, differential contact માટે નહીં.

ઉપયોગો

Suitable tray operation/inspection સાથે gas purification તથા recovery.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Pressure drop, foaming, corrosion, weeping તથા flooding limits છે. Approved hydraulic/pressure envelope જરૂરી છે.

4.12 • Packed Tower Absorber

વ્યાખ્યા

Wetted area પર differential interphase transfer આપવા packing ધરાવતો vertical gas–liquid contactor છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Wetted packing surfaces પર gas/liquid countercurrent contact કરે છે. Local driving force height પ્રમાણે બદલાય છે.

રચના (Construction)

Shell માં supports/hold-down સાથે random અથવા structured packing હોય છે. Top distributor lean solvent ફેલાવે છે. Deep bed માં redistributors હોઈ શકે છે. Gas packing નીચે enter થઈ top disengagement/mist-removal region માંથી બહાર જાય છે. Rich liquid bottom sump/outlet માં drain થાય છે. Packing area તથા void space આપે છે. Material, inspection તથા distribution nominal surface area જેટલાં મહત્વનાં છે.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Solvent films/rivulets તરીકે નીચે અને gas voids માંથી ઉપર જાય છે. Renewed interfaces પર gas solute liquid માં જાય છે. Bottom તરફ liquid rich તથા top તરફ gas lean થાય છે. Physical equilibrium trays નથી; active bed દરમિયાન composition સતત બદલાય છે. Poor distribution થી channeling/dry area તથા excessive loading થી pressure-drop/flooding થાય છે. Distributor liquid ને ફક્ત wall પાસે વહેવા દેવાને બદલે useful area જાળવે છે.

ઉપયોગો

High wetted area તથા ઘણી વખત low pressure drop યોગ્ય હોય તેવી absorption duties.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Maldistribution, fouling, plugging, foaming તથા flooding limits છે. ફક્ત packing choice performance ની ખાતરી નથી.

4.15 • Numerical:Minimum તથા Actual Solvent Ratio

આપેલ

Vs=100kmolh⁻¹, Yin=0.080, Yout=0.010, Xin=0. Solute-free basis નું given equilibriumY*=2X તથા bottom pinch controlling છે. Actual ratio minimum નું 1.40times લો.

શોધો

Minimum ratio, actual Ls તથા Xout શોધો.

Apparatus તથા તૈયારી

Approved gas/solvent, tower trainer, flowmeters, T/P indicators, gas analyzer તથા validated liquid assay લો. Supervised use પહેલાં diagram/ranges તપાસો.

Principle તથા Assumptions

Compatible molar-flow/composition basis પર component balance લો. Absorption થી total gas flow બદલાઈ શકે છે. Constant Vs માટે negligible inert dissolution/solvent evaporation જોઈએ.

Approved start/stop SOP હેઠળ assigned stable condition મેળવો. T/P, sample IDs તથા inlet/outlet compositions/flows નોંધો. Tower modify/enter કર્યા વગર pressure drop/distribution જુઓ. Gas loss ને liquid gain સામે compare કરો. Sample loss/reaction stoichiometry ગણો. Closure માટે readings બદલો નહીં.

વાઇવા પ્રશ્નો
1. Gas Absorption ના પ્રકાર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Gas mixture ના એક અથવા વધુ components ને contacting liquid solvent માં transfer કરવું એટલે gas absorption. Desorption/stripping તેની reverse transfer છે. Classification: physical absorption માં intended chemical reaction વગર gas dissolve થાય છે. Chemical absorption માં dissolution સાથે liquid reaction જોડાય છે. Single/multicomponent તથા batch/continuous independent classifications છે. Reaction driving force જાળવી શકે છે, પરંતુ reagent, heat, regeneration તથા reaction-equilibrium requirements ઉમેરે છે. Liquid bulk absorption ને solid-surface adsorption સાથે ન ભેળવો.

2. Absorption ના Industrial Applications ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Industrial absorption duty માં recover/remove કરવો તે gas solute, solvent તથા treated-gas/liquid-product quality નક્કી થાય છે. Ammonia ને water માં recover કરવું, suitable reactive solvent થી acid-gas treatment તથા process/off-gas ના soluble contaminants દૂર કરવાં examples છે. Solvent actual chemistry મુજબ જોઈએ; water universal solvent નથી. Reactive scrubber તથા physical solvent ના waste/regeneration loads જુદા છે. Absorber saleable solution, valuable-species recovery, downstream protection અથવા emission control માટે હોઈ શકે છે. Feed variation, heat release, mist, corrosion તથા solvent handling ફક્ત material balance થી solve થતા નથી.

3. Gas Solubility,Equilibrium તથા T/P ની અસર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Specified temperature, gas partial pressure તથા liquid composition પર equilibrium dissolved amount એટલે gas solubility. Henry’s law stated convention ધરાવતી dilute-solution equilibrium relation છે. Pressure-per-mole-fraction convention માં pA=HA xA એટલે yA*=HA xA/P લો. Fixed temperature પર solute partial pressure વધતાં physical solubility સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Gas mole fraction fixed રાખીને total pressure વધારવાથી partial pressure વધે છે; solute partial pressure fixed હોય તો સમાન solubility increase નહીં મળે. ઘણા physical systems માં dissolution exothermic હોવાથી temperature વધતાં solubility ઘટે છે, પરંતુ actual equilibrium data તપાસો. Reaction થી trend બદલાઈ શકે છે. Nonlinear/concentrated/reactive system માટે એક Henry constant સમગ્ર range માં valid ન હોઈ શકે.

4. Ideal Liquid Solution તથા Raoult’s Law ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Raoult standard-state basis પર activity coefficients unit હોય તે ideal liquid solution છે. Volatile liquid component ના equilibrium partial pressure ને liquid mole fraction તથા pure-component saturation pressure સાથે Raoult’s law જોડે છે. Fixed temperature પર ideal liquid તથા approximately ideal vapor માટે pA*=xA pA, sat છે. Saturation pressure temperature પર ખૂબ આધારિત છે. Equilibrium gas fraction pA*/P છે. દરેક sparingly soluble/reacting gas માટે આ universal law નથી; dilute solute માટે Henry standard state વધુ યોગ્ય હોઈ શકે છે. Ideal mixing એટલે બંને phases ની compositions સમાન નહીં. Ideal assumptions fail થાય તો activity/fugacity corrections જોઈએ.

5. Absorption Solvent ની પસંદગી ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

પૂરતી selective capacity સાથે circulation, separation, regeneration તથા safe handling માટે practical હોય તે suitable absorption solvent છે. Target-gas solubility/selectivity, low volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability તથા low corrosion જુઓ. Toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost તથા material compatibility સામેલ કરો. Regeneration energy તથા loaded-solvent treatment/disposal ગણો. Low volatility solvent loss ઘટાડે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping ને મદદ કરે છે પણ poor selectivity સુધારતી નથી. Reactive solvent માં heat removal તથા regeneration/reagent replacement જોઈએ. ફક્ત સૌથી ઊંચી equilibrium loading પરથી solvent ન પસંદ કરો.

6. Solute-free Material-balance Basis ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Solute-free flow એટલે nontransferring carrier gas અથવા solvent નો flow. Y તથા X અનુક્રમે carrier-gas mole તથા solvent mole દીઠ solute moles છે. એક-component transfer અને negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution તથા reaction માટે Vs, Ls constant રહે છે, જ્યારે total flows બદલાઈ શકે છે. Displayed solute-free conversion ratios dilute approximation સિવાય mole fractions સમાન નથી. બધા streams માટે same molar/time basis લો અને endpoints entering/exiting પ્રમાણે label કરો. Henry નું linear y*=mx exact solute-free X, Y માં linear નથી; converted relation અથવા સ્પષ્ટ dilute approximation લો.

7. HETP તથા તેનો યોગ્ય ઉપયોગ ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Specified conditions પર એક theoretical equilibrium stage જેટલું separation આપતી active packed height એટલે Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate, HETP. N theoretical stages જેટલા separation માટે active packed height Z=N×HETP છે. HETP physical tray spacing નથી તથા packing ની એકલ universal property નથી. Mixture, loading, wetting, distribution તથા conditions પર આધારિત છે. Distributors, demisters તથા disengagement માટે વધારાની જગ્યા હોવાથી total vessel height active packing કરતાં વધુ હોય છે. HETP ને height of transfer unit સાથે ન ભેળવો; અહીં syllabus મુજબ HETP છે.

8. Tray Tower Absorber ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Rising gas ને flowing liquid માં વારંવાર disperse કરવા trays ધરાવતો vertical gas–liquid contactor છે. દરેક tray પર interfacial contact થી soluble gas liquid તરફ transfer થાય છે. Successive trays stagewise countercurrent cascade બનાવે છે.

9. Packed Tower Absorber ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Wetted area પર differential interphase transfer આપવા packing ધરાવતો vertical gas–liquid contactor છે. Wetted packing surfaces પર gas/liquid countercurrent contact કરે છે. Local driving force height પ્રમાણે બદલાય છે.
