4. Gas AbsorptionMass Transfer-I • DI04005021 • Chemical Semester4 • 8h / 18% • GTU2025-26
Syllabus according to detailed theory, derivations, equipment construction and working and worked numericals. Practicals carry official suggested exercises and blank observation sheets — no fabricated results.
4. Notes
4.1 • Types of gas absorption

Definition / principle

Gas absorption transfers one or more components of a gas mixture into a contacting liquid solvent; desorption or stripping is the reverse transfer.

Detailed theory and conditions

Classification first: physical absorption dissolves a gas without an intended chemical reaction; chemical absorption couples dissolution with reaction in the liquid. Absorption may be single-component or multicomponent and batch or continuous. These are independent classifications. Chemical reaction can maintain a stronger driving force, but adds reagent demand, heat, regeneration and reaction-equilibrium requirements. Do not confuse absorption into a liquid bulk with adsorption onto a solid surface.

4.2 • Industrial applications of absorption

Definition / principle

An industrial absorption duty specifies the gas solute to recover or remove, the solvent and the required treated-gas and liquid-product quality.

Detailed theory and conditions

Examples include ammonia recovery into water, acid-gas treatment using a suitable reactive solvent and removal of soluble contaminants from process/off-gases. The solvent must match the actual gas chemistry: water is not universally suitable and a reactive scrubbing liquid produces a different waste/regeneration load from a physical solvent. The absorber may make a saleable solution, recover a valuable species, protect downstream equipment or meet emission targets. Feed variability, heat release, entrained mist, corrosion and solvent handling are part of the duty, not matters solved by a material balance alone.

4.3 • Gas solubility,equilibrium and effects of T/P

Definition / principle

Gas solubility is the equilibrium dissolved amount under specified temperature, gas partial pressure and liquid composition. Henry’s law is a dilute-solution equilibrium relation with a stated convention.

Detailed theory and conditions

Use pA=HA xA in the pressure-per-mole-fraction convention; then yA*=HA xA/P. Higher solute partial pressure normally increases physical gas solubility at fixed temperature. Increasing total pressure at fixed gas mole fraction raises partial pressure; increasing total pressure while holding solute partial pressure fixed does not give the same solubility increase. For many physically absorbed gases, raising temperature reduces solubility because dissolution is exothermic, but the actual gas/solvent equilibrium data must decide; chemical reactions can change the trend. Nonlinear, concentrated or reactive systems may not obey a single Henry constant over the full range.

Equations and notation

4.4 • Ideal liquid solution and Raoult’s law

Definition / principle

An ideal liquid solution has unit activity coefficients on the Raoult-standard-state basis. Raoult’s law relates a volatile liquid component’s equilibrium partial pressure to its liquid mole fraction and pure-component saturation pressure.

Detailed theory and conditions

At a fixed temperature, pA*=xA pA, sat for an ideal liquid and an approximately ideal vapor. The saturation pressure depends strongly on temperature. The equilibrium gas fraction is pA*/P. The rule is not a universal solubility equation for every sparingly soluble or reacting gas; Henry’s dilute-solute standard state may be the appropriate description instead. Ideal mixing does not mean the contacting phases have identical compositions. A real activity coefficient or fugacity correction is needed when the stated ideal approximations fail.

Equations and notation

4.5 • Choice of absorption solvent

Definition / principle

A suitable absorption solvent provides sufficient selective capacity while remaining practical to circulate, separate, regenerate and handle safely.

Detailed theory and conditions

Consider high target-gas solubility/selectivity, low solvent volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability and low corrosiveness. Include toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost and compatibility with construction materials. Evaluate regeneration energy and the disposal/treatment of loaded solvent. Low volatility reduces solvent loss to gas; low viscosity aids transfer and pumping but cannot override poor selectivity. A reactive solvent may capture strongly while requiring heat removal and regeneration or reagent replacement. Do not select a solvent solely from the highest single equilibrium loading.

4.6 • Solute-free material-balance basis

Definition / principle

A solute-free flow is the flow of nontransferring carrier gas or solvent. Solute ratios Y and X are moles of solute per mole of carrier gas and solvent, respectively.

Detailed theory and conditions

For one-component transfer with negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution and reaction, Vs and Ls remain constant even though total gas and liquid flows change. The displayed solute-free conversion ratios are not equal to mole fractions except approximately for dilute streams. Use the same molar time basis in all streams and label entering/exiting endpoints rather than relying on ambiguous subscripts. Henry’s linear y*=mx is not exactly linear in solute-free X, Y; use a converted relation or a clearly stated dilute approximation.

Equations and notation

4.7 • Derivation:countercurrent absorber material balance

Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, one transferred solute; constant carrier flows Vs and Ls; negligible solvent volatility and inert-gas dissolution. All X, Y are solute-free molar ratios.

  1. Overall solute balance: gas enters rich and leaves lean; liquid enters lean and leaves rich.

  2. Rearrange to amount transferred.

  3. Take a top-to-local-section balance. Gas leaving the top has Yout and liquid entering the top has Xin.

  4. Obtain the positive-slope operating line. Endpoints are (Xin, Yout) and (Xout, Yin).

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: stream labels → overall balance → rearrange → operating-line endpoints. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

4.8 • Derivation:co-current absorber material balance

Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, one transferred solute; constant carrier flows Vs and Ls; negligible solvent volatility and inert-gas dissolution. All X, Y are solute-free molar ratios.

  1. Both streams enter the same end with Yin and Xin.

  2. Rearrange at any common position.

  3. The local operating line has negative slope on this X, Y plot.

  4. At the common outlet the overall transferred amount is unchanged in balance form, but endpoint pairing and achievable approach differ.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: common inlet → local balance → negative operating-line slope → outlet balance. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

4.9 • Derivation:minimum liquid-to-gas ratio

Symbols, model and assumptions

Use the preceding constant-carrier countercurrent model. Specified Yin, Yout and Xin; given equilibrium curve. A bottom pinch formula is valid only when that pinch controls. Check interior tangency and the whole operating range.

  1. Start from the overall transfer balance.

  2. Minimum solvent corresponds to the largest thermodynamically admissible outlet loading for a bottom-controlled pinch.

  3. Insert the limiting loading.

  4. Only if the given equilibrium model is linear in solute-free ratios, solve Xout, max explicitly.

  5. At minimum a pinch eliminates local driving force and finite-rate equipment becomes unbounded in the ideal model. Actual ratio must exceed the feasible minimum.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: overall balance → identify controlling equilibrium pinch → limiting ratio; qualify bottom-pinch assumption. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

4.10 • HETP and its proper use

Definition / principle

Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate is the active packed height that gives separation equivalent to one theoretical equilibrium stage for specified conditions.

Detailed theory and conditions

If N theoretical stages represent a specified packed-bed separation, active packed height Z=N×HETP. HETP is a performance equivalence, not the physical tray spacing and not a universal property of packing alone. It depends on the mixture, loading, wetting, distribution and operating conditions. Overall vessel height includes additional space for distributors, demisters and disengagement, so it is larger than the active packed height. HETP should not be confused with a height of transfer unit; the syllabus asks HETP, not an unrelated full HTU/NTU design derivation.

Equations and notation

4.11 • Tray tower absorber

Definition

A vertical gas–liquid contactor with trays that repeatedly disperse rising gas through flowing liquid.

Principle

Interfacial contact on each tray transfers soluble gas toward the liquid; successive trays approximate a stagewise countercurrent cascade.

Construction

The vertical shell contains horizontal trays with gas passages, liquid weirs and downcomers. A sieve-tray arrangement is illustrated; valve and bubble-cap trays are alternatives. The gas inlet is near the bottom and lean solvent enters above the upper tray. Treated gas leaves the top, commonly through a mist eliminator, while rich liquid leaves a bottom sump. Downcomer outlets maintain suitable liquid seals, and access/supports allow inspection. Trays provide distinct contacting levels rather than a continuous packed surface.

Working

Rising gas passes through tray openings and bubbles through the retained liquid. Liquid flows across a tray, over its weir and down the downcomer to the next lower tray. Solute crosses the gas–liquid interface, so gas becomes leaner upward and liquid richer downward. Sufficient gas supports effective contact; too little can cause weeping, whereas excessive gas/liquid loading can cause entrainment or flooding. Actual tray departures need not reach equilibrium. Although both feeds flow continuously, the contacting is stagewise; the syllabus grouping under continuous equipment refers to throughput, not differential contact.

Applications

Gas purification/recovery where tray operation, inspection and staged contact are suitable.

Limitations and precautions

Pressure drop, foaming, corrosion, weeping and flooding limit operation; equipment must remain within its approved hydraulic and pressure envelope.

4.12 • Packed tower absorber

Definition

A vertical gas–liquid contactor containing packing that supplies wetted area for differential interphase transfer.

Principle

Gas and liquid contact countercurrently over distributed wetted packing surfaces; local driving force changes with height.

Construction

The shell contains random or structured packing retained by supports and hold-down arrangements. A top liquid distributor spreads lean solvent; redistributors may serve deep beds. Gas enters below the packing and leaves above it through a disengagement/mist-removal region. Rich liquid drains into a bottom sump and outlet. Packing must provide area and void space without blocking phase passage. Appropriate materials, inspection access and distribution are as important as nominal surface area.

Working

Solvent flows downward as films and rivulets while gas rises through the voids. Soluble gas transfers across repeatedly renewed interfaces; the liquid gains solute toward the bottom and gas loses solute toward the top. There are no physical equilibrium trays, so composition varies progressively along the active bed. Poor distribution creates channeling and dry areas, while excessive loading raises pressure drop and can flood the bed. Distributors therefore maintain useful area rather than allowing liquid to run only near the wall.

Applications

Absorption duties benefiting from high wetted area and often relatively low pressure drop.

Limitations and precautions

Maldistribution, fouling, plugging, foaming and flooding are limitations. Packing choice alone does not guarantee mass-transfer performance.

Solved numericals and practicals
Rate of gas absorption in a packed tower

Objective and official scope

Find the absorbed-solute molar rate from measured steady gas/liquid streams in the approved packed-tower trainer.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved gas/solvent system, tower trainer, flowmeters, T/P indicators, gas-composition analyzer and validated liquid assay. Inspect the trainer diagram and range before supervised use.

Principle and assumptions

Use component balances with compatible molar flow and composition bases. Total gas flow may change as solute is absorbed. Constant inert-carrier Vs requires negligible inert dissolution/solvent evaporation.

Procedure and record

Under the approved start-up/shutdown SOP establish the assigned stable operating condition. Record both inlet/outlet compositions and calibrated flows with T/P and sample IDs. Observe pressure drop and liquid distribution without entering or modifying the tower. Compare gas loss with liquid gain, accounting for sample losses and any reaction stoichiometry. Report discrepancies rather than adjusting readings to force closure.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Use only the institution-approved gas and treatment/vent system. No toxic-gas generation, pressurization or live valve changes outside the supervised SOP. A rate balance alone does not give a mass-transfer coefficient without area/driving-force information.

Viva questions
1. Define and explain the principle of Types of gas absorption.

Gas absorption transfers one or more components of a gas mixture into a contacting liquid solvent; desorption or stripping is the reverse transfer. Classification first: physical absorption dissolves a gas without an intended chemical reaction; chemical absorption couples dissolution with reaction in the liquid. Absorption may be single-component or multicomponent and batch or continuous. These are independent classifications. Chemical reaction can maintain a stronger driving force, but adds reagent demand, heat, regeneration and reaction-equilibrium requirements. Do not confuse absorption into a liquid bulk with adsorption onto a solid surface.

2. Define and explain the principle of Industrial applications of absorption.

An industrial absorption duty specifies the gas solute to recover or remove, the solvent and the required treated-gas and liquid-product quality. Examples include ammonia recovery into water, acid-gas treatment using a suitable reactive solvent and removal of soluble contaminants from process/off-gases. The solvent must match the actual gas chemistry: water is not universally suitable and a reactive scrubbing liquid produces a different waste/regeneration load from a physical solvent. The absorber may make a saleable solution, recover a valuable species, protect downstream equipment or meet emission targets. Feed variability, heat release, entrained mist, corrosion and solvent handling are part of the duty, not matters solved by a material balance alone.

3. Define and explain the principle of Gas solubility,equilibrium and effects of T/P.

Gas solubility is the equilibrium dissolved amount under specified temperature, gas partial pressure and liquid composition. Henry’s law is a dilute-solution equilibrium relation with a stated convention. Use pA=HA xA in the pressure-per-mole-fraction convention; then yA*=HA xA/P. Higher solute partial pressure normally increases physical gas solubility at fixed temperature. Increasing total pressure at fixed gas mole fraction raises partial pressure; increasing total pressure while holding solute partial pressure fixed does not give the same solubility increase. For many physically absorbed gases, raising temperature reduces solubility because dissolution is exothermic, but the actual gas/solvent equilibrium data must decide; chemical reactions can change the trend. Nonlinear, concentrated or reactive systems may not obey a single Henry constant over the full range.

4. Define and explain the principle of Ideal liquid solution and Raoult’s law.

An ideal liquid solution has unit activity coefficients on the Raoult-standard-state basis. Raoult’s law relates a volatile liquid component’s equilibrium partial pressure to its liquid mole fraction and pure-component saturation pressure. At a fixed temperature, pA*=xA pA, sat for an ideal liquid and an approximately ideal vapor. The saturation pressure depends strongly on temperature. The equilibrium gas fraction is pA*/P. The rule is not a universal solubility equation for every sparingly soluble or reacting gas; Henry’s dilute-solute standard state may be the appropriate description instead. Ideal mixing does not mean the contacting phases have identical compositions. A real activity coefficient or fugacity correction is needed when the stated ideal approximations fail.

5. Define and explain the principle of Choice of absorption solvent.

A suitable absorption solvent provides sufficient selective capacity while remaining practical to circulate, separate, regenerate and handle safely. Consider high target-gas solubility/selectivity, low solvent volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability and low corrosiveness. Include toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost and compatibility with construction materials. Evaluate regeneration energy and the disposal/treatment of loaded solvent. Low volatility reduces solvent loss to gas; low viscosity aids transfer and pumping but cannot override poor selectivity. A reactive solvent may capture strongly while requiring heat removal and regeneration or reagent replacement. Do not select a solvent solely from the highest single equilibrium loading.

6. Define and explain the principle of Solute-free material-balance basis.

A solute-free flow is the flow of nontransferring carrier gas or solvent. Solute ratios Y and X are moles of solute per mole of carrier gas and solvent, respectively. For one-component transfer with negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution and reaction, Vs and Ls remain constant even though total gas and liquid flows change. The displayed solute-free conversion ratios are not equal to mole fractions except approximately for dilute streams. Use the same molar time basis in all streams and label entering/exiting endpoints rather than relying on ambiguous subscripts. Henry’s linear y*=mx is not exactly linear in solute-free X, Y; use a converted relation or a clearly stated dilute approximation.

7. Define and explain the principle of HETP and its proper use.

Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate is the active packed height that gives separation equivalent to one theoretical equilibrium stage for specified conditions. If N theoretical stages represent a specified packed-bed separation, active packed height Z=N×HETP. HETP is a performance equivalence, not the physical tray spacing and not a universal property of packing alone. It depends on the mixture, loading, wetting, distribution and operating conditions. Overall vessel height includes additional space for distributors, demisters and disengagement, so it is larger than the active packed height. HETP should not be confused with a height of transfer unit; the syllabus asks HETP, not an unrelated full HTU/NTU design derivation.

8. Define and explain the principle of Tray tower absorber.

A vertical gas–liquid contactor with trays that repeatedly disperse rising gas through flowing liquid. Interfacial contact on each tray transfers soluble gas toward the liquid; successive trays approximate a stagewise countercurrent cascade.

9. Define and explain the principle of Packed tower absorber.

A vertical gas–liquid contactor containing packing that supplies wetted area for differential interphase transfer. Gas and liquid contact countercurrently over distributed wetted packing surfaces; local driving force changes with height.

5. Liquid–Liquid ExtractionMass Transfer-I • DI04005021 • Chemical Semester4 • 10h / 22% • GTU2025-26
Syllabus મુજબ વિગતવાર Theory, derivations, equipment ના Construction/Working તથા worked Numericals. Practical માં official suggested exercises તથા blank observation sheets છે—fabricated results નથી.
5. નોટ્સ
5.1 • Liquid–liquid Extraction તથા Industrial Uses

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Original liquid તથા બીજો solvent બે separable phases બનાવે અને solute તેમના વચ્ચે distribute થાય તે liquid–liquid extraction છે. Solvent-rich product extract અને feed-carrier-rich product raffinate છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Volatility difference ઓછો હોય, heat-sensitive material હોય અથવા solvent useful selectivity આપે ત્યારે extraction ઉપયોગી છે. Aqueous streams માંથી organic acids recovery, chemical purification તથા suitable extractants વડે hydrometallurgical extraction examples છે. Downstream solvent recovery સામાન્ય રીતે જોઈએ; extraction માત્રથી pure solute મળતો નથી. Light phase હંમેશાં extract નથી. Extract solvent identity પરથી અને top/bottom density પરથી નક્કી થાય છે.

5.2 • Liquid Equilibrium,Distribution તથા Selectivity

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Given T, P પર બે coexisting liquid phases ની compositions liquid equilibrium દર્શાવે છે. Conjugate equilibrium compositions જોડતી line tie line છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Declared basis પર extract તથા raffinate માં solute concentrations નો ratio distribution coefficient છે. Composition, T તથા association થી તે બદલાઈ શકે છે; universal constant નથી. Selectivity phases વચ્ચે solute C ને carrier A સામે અલગ કરવાની ક્ષમતા દર્શાવે છે. High-capacity solvent carrier પણ ઘણો dissolve કરે તો selectivity નબળી હોઈ શકે છે. બે phases હોવી જરૂરી છે. એક homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture થી interphase coefficient નક્કી ન થાય. Aqueous તથા organic phases સ્પષ્ટ ઓળખો.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

5.3 • Equilateral Triangular Coordinates તથા Lever Rule

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

ત્રણ components ના fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોય તેવી compositions equilateral ternary diagram દર્શાવે છે. Vertex pure component તથા opposite side તે component નો zero fraction છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Vertex ની opposite side ને parallel lines વડે fraction વાંચો. Component names, T તથા mass/mole basis લખો; બંને bases mix ન કરો. Binary mixture edge પર અને ternary mixture અંદર આવે છે. F તથા S નું mixing point M straight joining line પર તથા larger stream ની નજીક આવે છે. M ના E, R products measured tie line પર હોય છે; vertex તરફ arbitrary line નહીં. Lever rule માં opposite segment lengths નો ratio લેવાય છે. Mixing line તથા equilibrium tie line જુદાં છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

5.4 • Three Liquids:One Partially Soluble Pair તથા T/P અસર

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Stated range માં એક binary pair limited mutual solubility ધરાવે અને third component બંને સાથે miscible હોય તે Type-I ternary system છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Partially miscible pair થી miscibility gap બને છે; તેની ternary boundary binodal curve છે. Two-phase region નું mixture tie line અનુસાર split થાય છે. Plait point પાસે બંને phases નો difference અદૃશ્ય થાય છે. Tie lines હંમેશાં horizontal નથી; actual data જોઈએ. ઘણા upper-critical systems માં heating થી gap ઘટે છે, પરંતુ lower-critical/complex behavior પણ હોય છે. Temperature થી miscibility હંમેશાં વધે એવું ન કહો. Nearly incompressible liquids પર ordinary pressure ની અસર સામાન્ય રીતે ઓછી છે; high pressure/gas solubility/special behavior exceptions છે. આ schematic છે, measured acid/benzene/water data નથી.

5.5 • Three Liquids:Two Partially Soluble Pairs

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified conditions પર બે binary pairs limited mutual solubility ધરાવે તે Type-II ternary system છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

બે binary edges પર miscibility gaps મળે છે. Two-phase region તથા conjugate branches actual equilibrium data પરથી નક્કી કરો; તે Type-I cap/plait construction જેવી હોવી જરૂરી નથી. Tie lines coexisting phases જોડે છે અને phase fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોવો જોઈએ. બે partially miscible binary pairs એટલે ત્રણ liquid phases નહીં. Sketch બે affected edges ઓળખાવે છે; quantitative stage compositions માટે data નથી.

5.6 • Extraction Solvent ની પસંદગી

વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Favorable solute distribution તથા separable phases સાથે recoverable અને safe હોય તે extraction solvent પસંદ કરવો.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Selectivity, capacity, feed carrier સાથે mutual solubility, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, stability તથા regeneration જુઓ. Density difference settling ને મદદ કરે છે. Stable emulsion/low interfacial tension disengagement મુશ્કેલ કરી શકે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping સુધારે છે પણ solvent loss/contamination ખર્ચાળ હોઈ શકે છે. Toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost તથા compatibility ગણો. High distribution coefficient માત્ર પૂરતો નથી.

5.7 • Derivation:Single-stage Extraction Balance તથા Lever Rule

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady equilibrium stage અથવા completed batch, no reaction/evaporation. F, S, E, R same-basis masses/mass rates છે. zF, zS, zM તથા wE, wR solute mass fractions છે. Equilibrium endpoints અલગથી જાણીતા હોવા જોઈએ.

  1. Total balance તથા mixed composition.

  2. Phase separation પછી component balance.

  3. Raffinate flow eliminate કરો.

  4. બંને product flows શોધો.

  5. E–R tie line માટે lever rule મેળવો.

  6. Carrier તથા solvent balances પણ close કરો. Inconsistent ternary endpoints માટે solute-only result પૂરતો નથી.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

5.8 • Derivation:Multistage Crosscurrent Extraction

સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

પહેલાં general stage balances લો. Closed form માટે constant insoluble carrier L, pure fresh solvent Sj, negligible mutual solubility તથા solute-free mass ratios પર Yj=mXj લો. X=solute/carrier, Y=solute/solvent છે.

  1. Stage j ના general total તથા solute balances.

  2. Total raffinate constant માન્યા વગર component balance.

  3. Stated carrier model માં pure solvent નું entering solute zero છે.

  4. Equilibrium ratio મૂકી solve કરો.

  5. Successive fresh-solvent contacts ના residual factors multiply કરો.

  6. Equal solvent portions તથા constant m માટે residual પરથી recovery મેળવો.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

5.9 • Agitated Extraction Vessel

વ્યાખ્યા

એક liquid phase ને બીજામાં disperse કરીને extraction contact આપતું mechanically mixed vessel છે. Phase separation થી stage પૂર્ણ થાય છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Agitation interfacial area વધારી liquid films renew કરે છે; solute equilibrium distribution તરફ જાય છે.

રચના (Construction)

Vessel માં driven shaft/impeller, baffles, feed/solvent connections તથા contacted-mixture outlet હોય છે. Compatible seal/containment solvent escape limit કરે છે. Batch માં agitation બંધ કર્યા પછી settling એ જ vessel માં થઈ શકે છે. Continuous mixer ની dispersion સામાન્ય રીતે separate gravity settler માં જાય છે. Mixer outlet બે-phase mixture છે; પોતે separated products નથી.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Feed તથા solvent controlled mixing હેઠળ મળે છે. એક phase ના droplets બીજી phase માં બની enlarged interface પરથી transfer થાય છે. Required residence time રાખો; vigorous mixing એટલે equilibrium ની ખાતરી નહીં. Dispersion settle કર્યા પછી phases અલગ withdraw થાય છે. Batch માં mixing/settling alternate થાય છે; continuous mixer–settler માં adjacent units આ functions જુદાં કરે છે. Excessive shear stable emulsions/carryover વધારી શકે છે.

ઉપયોગો

Stagewise extraction તથા mixer–settler cascade નો mixer section.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Power, sealing, emulsification તથા residence time મહત્વનાં છે. Actual use માટે hazardous-solvent SOP તથા rated containment જરૂરી છે.

5.10 • Gravity Settler

વ્યાખ્યા

Gravity વડે contacted dispersion ને light/heavy liquid layers માં અલગ કરતું low-velocity vessel છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Density difference થી droplets rise/settle તથા coalesce થાય છે; પૂરતો disengagement time જોઈએ.

રચના (Construction)

Horizontal chamber માં calming inlet/baffle, quiet volume, interface region તથા separate light/heavy outlets અને level/interface control હોય છે. Compatible duty માટે coalescing internals હોઈ શકે છે; તે residence time નો વિકલ્પ નથી. Drawing light/heavy outlets બતાવે છે. Extract/raffinate identity solvent-rich layer મુજબ નક્કી થાય છે.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Mixed dispersion vessel માં ધીમી પડે છે. Droplets gravity હેઠળ move/coalesce થઈ interface બનાવે છે. Light liquid ઉપરથી અને heavy liquid નીચેથી નીકળે છે; outlets phase inventories જાળવે છે. Settling extraction contact પછીની separation step છે; તે equilibrium transfer ની આપોઆપ ખાતરી નથી. Fine stable emulsion માટે જુદી contacting/separation conditions જરૂરી થઈ શકે છે; વધુ outlet rate solution નથી.

ઉપયોગો

Mixer–settler extraction તથા solvent-recovery માં phase disengagement.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Small density difference, high viscosity તથા emulsion માટે વધુ area/time જોઈએ. Interface control cross-contamination ઘટાડે છે.

5.11 • Sieve-tray Extraction Tower

વ્યાખ્યા

Perforated trays વડે એક liquid ને બીજી liquid માં droplets તરીકે distribute કરતો extraction column છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Repeated droplet formation/contact તથા redistribution થી countercurrent liquids વચ્ચે interfacial transfer વધે છે.

રચના (Construction)

Shell માં perforated trays તથા opposite continuous phase માટે passages/downcomers છે. Drawing માં light dispersed solvent નીચેથી આવી holes માંથી ઊઠે છે. Heavy feed ઉપરથી designated passages માં નીચે જાય છે. End disengagement sections તથા interface controls separated phases એકત્ર કરે છે. Tray spacing/open area loading નક્કી કરે છે. અહીં liquid droplets છે, absorber જેવા gas bubbles નહીં.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Light phase holes માંથી dispersed droplets બનાવે છે. Droplet travel તથા successive tray contacts દરમિયાન solute phases વચ્ચે distribute થાય છે. Heavy liquid નીચે અને light droplets ઉપર જાય છે. Top/bottom separation zones થી products withdraw થાય છે. Physical stages છે, દરેક ideal હોવો જરૂરી નથી. Density/continuous-phase choice બદલાય તો ports/hydraulics પણ accordingly બદલવા પડે છે.

ઉપયોગો

Suitable tray hydraulics/density difference ધરાવતી countercurrent extraction.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Flooding, phase inversion, entrainment તથા emulsion useful throughput limit કરે છે.

5.12 • Packed Extraction Tower

વ્યાખ્યા

Column height દરમિયાન contacting liquids distribute કરવા packing વાપરતો differential extractor છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Countercurrent liquid flow તથા wetting/droplet renewal discrete equilibrium trays વગર transfer આપે છે.

રચના (Construction)

Vertical shell માં compatible packing, supports, phase distributors તથા enlarged end disengagement zones છે. Drawing ના light-solvent case માં heavy feed bed ઉપર અને light solvent નીચે enter થાય છે. Light/heavy outlets પર interface control છે. Actual liquids મુજબ packing wetting તથા continuous/dispersed phase પસંદ થાય છે. તે ફક્ત gas absorber ના stream names બદલેલી arrangement નથી.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Light solvent packing માંથી ઉપર તથા heavy liquid નીચે જાય છે. Bed દરમિયાન solute transfer અને ends પર disengagement થાય છે. આ example માં solvent-rich extract light end અને carrier-rich raffinate heavy end પરથી નીકળે છે. Solvent density reverse હોય તો product positions reverse થાય છે. Maldistribution useful area ઘટાડે છે; excessive loading entrainment, flooding અથવા phase inversion કરે છે.

ઉપયોગો

Clean liquids તથા favorable distribution/wetting માટે continuous extraction.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Fouling, emulsion, poor wetting તથા small density difference duty ને unsuitable બનાવી શકે છે.

5.13 • Rotating Disk Contactor (RDC)

વ્યાખ્યા

Rotating disks તથા stationary rings ધરાવતો mechanically agitated vertical extraction column છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Controlled mechanical dispersion interfaces renew કરે છે અને countercurrent flow concentration progression આપે છે.

રચના (Construction)

Column ના central driven shaft પર spaced circular disks તથા shell પર stationary ring baffles છે. Contacting section માં feed/solvent inlets તથા ends પર disengagement/outlet/interface control છે. Motor તથા suitable shaft seal rotor ચલાવે છે. Stator rings circulation regions બનાવે છે તથા excessive axial mixing limit કરે છે. Disks perforated equilibrium trays નથી.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Rotor phases ને shear/circulate કરીને useful droplets તથા renewed films બનાવે છે. Heavy/light streams opposite direction માં agitated regions પાર કરે છે અને solute distribute થાય છે. End zones dispersion ધીમી કરી withdrawal પહેલાં separation આપે છે. Speed થી droplet size, holdup, power તથા axial mixing બદલાય છે. Speed સતત વધારવાથી emulsion/flooding થઈ શકે છે. Actual equilibrium તથા residence-time/efficiency data જોઈએ.

ઉપયોગો

Controlled mechanical dispersion જરૂરી હોય તેવી continuous extraction.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Moving parts, seals, power, axial mixing તથા emulsion sensitivity માટે suitable design/maintenance જોઈએ.

5.14 • Centrifugal Extractor

વ્યાખ્યા

Liquid–liquid contacting તથા centrifugal acceleration હેઠળ phase separation જોડતું compact contactor છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Mixing transfer વધારેછે; rotation density-based separation ઝડપી બનાવે છે, પણ પોતે equilibrium selectivity બદલતું નથી.

રચના (Construction)

Representative unit માં stationary housing, two feeds, mixing region, rotating separating bowl તથા internal weirs/passages દ્વારા separate outlets છે. Motor, shaft, bearings તથા seals rotor support કરે છે. Sketch heavy outer તથા light inner layer જુદા બતાવે છે. Exact arrangements design-dependent છે. Balanced rotor તથા rated containment જરૂરી છે.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Feed/solvent ની contacted dispersion માં solute distribution relation તરફ જાય છે. Rotating zone માં denser liquid બહાર તથા lighter liquid અંદર જાય છે. Designated outlet paths અલગ products આપે છે. Gravity settling કરતાં separation ઝડપી થઈ શકે છે. એક centrifugal unit આપોઆપ ઘણા ideal stages નથી; greater recovery/purity માટે units cascade થાય છે. Solids, unstable hydraulics અથવા poor mixing performance limit કરે છે.

ઉપયોગો

Rotor-compatible fluids માટે compact extraction, short residence-time તથા difficult gravity disengagement duties.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Rotor balance, speed rating, seals, power તથા solids tolerance મહત્વનાં છે. Study sketch પરથી safe limits ન નક્કી કરો.

Apparatus તથા તૈયારી

Institution-approved phase pairs/assays લો. Commonly aqueous acid તથા selected organic solvent separate experiments માં હોય છે, પણ actual composition/method manual માં confirm થવી જોઈએ.

ફક્ત toluene+acid અથવા chloroform+acid ને આપોઆપ two-phase ન માનો. KD માટે identified coexisting phases તથા declared concentration basis જરૂરી છે.

Approved equilibrium/settling/sampling method અનુસરો. Recorded T પર બંને phases માં acid assay કરો. Same mass-fraction અથવા molar-concentration basis પર KD ગણો. Suggested Activity તથા Evidence

Approved non-working contactor model બનાવો. Phase paths, internals તથા purpose label કરો. Live pressure/heat/solvent operation ઉમેરશો નહીં.

Equilateral ternary coordinates:declared mass-fraction basis—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Type-I liquid equilibrium:binodal,tie lines and plait point—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Type-II topology:two partially miscible pairs,not three phases—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Single equilibrium extraction stage:mix,contact and separate—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Crosscurrent extraction:fresh solvent to each raffinate stage—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Agitated vessel:mixing does not itself separate product phases—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Gravity settler:phase disengagement after mixing—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Sieve-tray extractor:light droplets rise,heavy phase descends—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Packed liquid extractor:two liquid phases,not gas/liquid—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Rotating disk contactor:rotor disks and stator rings—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

Centrifugal extractor:mixing followed by rotating phase separation—labelled અભ્યાસચિત્ર

વાઇવા પ્રશ્નો
1. Liquid–liquid Extraction તથા Industrial Uses ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Original liquid તથા બીજો solvent બે separable phases બનાવે અને solute તેમના વચ્ચે distribute થાય તે liquid–liquid extraction છે. Solvent-rich product extract અને feed-carrier-rich product raffinate છે. Volatility difference ઓછો હોય, heat-sensitive material હોય અથવા solvent useful selectivity આપે ત્યારે extraction ઉપયોગી છે. Aqueous streams માંથી organic acids recovery, chemical purification તથા suitable extractants વડે hydrometallurgical extraction examples છે. Downstream solvent recovery સામાન્ય રીતે જોઈએ; extraction માત્રથી pure solute મળતો નથી. Light phase હંમેશાં extract નથી. Extract solvent identity પરથી અને top/bottom density પરથી નક્કી થાય છે.

2. Liquid Equilibrium,Distribution તથા Selectivity ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Given T, P પર બે coexisting liquid phases ની compositions liquid equilibrium દર્શાવે છે. Conjugate equilibrium compositions જોડતી line tie line છે. Declared basis પર extract તથા raffinate માં solute concentrations નો ratio distribution coefficient છે. Composition, T તથા association થી તે બદલાઈ શકે છે; universal constant નથી. Selectivity phases વચ્ચે solute C ને carrier A સામે અલગ કરવાની ક્ષમતા દર્શાવે છે. High-capacity solvent carrier પણ ઘણો dissolve કરે તો selectivity નબળી હોઈ શકે છે. બે phases હોવી જરૂરી છે. એક homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture થી interphase coefficient નક્કી ન થાય. Aqueous તથા organic phases સ્પષ્ટ ઓળખો.

3. Equilateral Triangular Coordinates તથા Lever Rule ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

ત્રણ components ના fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોય તેવી compositions equilateral ternary diagram દર્શાવે છે. Vertex pure component તથા opposite side તે component નો zero fraction છે. Vertex ની opposite side ને parallel lines વડે fraction વાંચો. Component names, T તથા mass/mole basis લખો; બંને bases mix ન કરો. Binary mixture edge પર અને ternary mixture અંદર આવે છે. F તથા S નું mixing point M straight joining line પર તથા larger stream ની નજીક આવે છે. M ના E, R products measured tie line પર હોય છે; vertex તરફ arbitrary line નહીં. Lever rule માં opposite segment lengths નો ratio લેવાય છે. Mixing line તથા equilibrium tie line જુદાં છે.

4. Three Liquids:One Partially Soluble Pair તથા T/P અસર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Stated range માં એક binary pair limited mutual solubility ધરાવે અને third component બંને સાથે miscible હોય તે Type-I ternary system છે. Partially miscible pair થી miscibility gap બને છે; તેની ternary boundary binodal curve છે. Two-phase region નું mixture tie line અનુસાર split થાય છે. Plait point પાસે બંને phases નો difference અદૃશ્ય થાય છે. Tie lines હંમેશાં horizontal નથી; actual data જોઈએ. ઘણા upper-critical systems માં heating થી gap ઘટે છે, પરંતુ lower-critical/complex behavior પણ હોય છે. Temperature થી miscibility હંમેશાં વધે એવું ન કહો. Nearly incompressible liquids પર ordinary pressure ની અસર સામાન્ય રીતે ઓછી છે; high pressure/gas solubility/special behavior exceptions છે. આ schematic છે, measured acid/benzene/water data નથી.

5. Three Liquids:Two Partially Soluble Pairs ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Specified conditions પર બે binary pairs limited mutual solubility ધરાવે તે Type-II ternary system છે. બે binary edges પર miscibility gaps મળે છે. Two-phase region તથા conjugate branches actual equilibrium data પરથી નક્કી કરો; તે Type-I cap/plait construction જેવી હોવી જરૂરી નથી. Tie lines coexisting phases જોડે છે અને phase fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોવો જોઈએ. બે partially miscible binary pairs એટલે ત્રણ liquid phases નહીં. Sketch બે affected edges ઓળખાવે છે; quantitative stage compositions માટે data નથી.

6. Extraction Solvent ની પસંદગી ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Favorable solute distribution તથા separable phases સાથે recoverable અને safe હોય તે extraction solvent પસંદ કરવો. Selectivity, capacity, feed carrier સાથે mutual solubility, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, stability તથા regeneration જુઓ. Density difference settling ને મદદ કરે છે. Stable emulsion/low interfacial tension disengagement મુશ્કેલ કરી શકે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping સુધારે છે પણ solvent loss/contamination ખર્ચાળ હોઈ શકે છે. Toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost તથા compatibility ગણો. High distribution coefficient માત્ર પૂરતો નથી.

7. Agitated Extraction Vessel ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

એક liquid phase ને બીજામાં disperse કરીને extraction contact આપતું mechanically mixed vessel છે. Phase separation થી stage પૂર્ણ થાય છે. Agitation interfacial area વધારી liquid films renew કરે છે; solute equilibrium distribution તરફ જાય છે.

8. Gravity Settler ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Gravity વડે contacted dispersion ને light/heavy liquid layers માં અલગ કરતું low-velocity vessel છે. Density difference થી droplets rise/settle તથા coalesce થાય છે; પૂરતો disengagement time જોઈએ.

9. Sieve-tray Extraction Tower ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Perforated trays વડે એક liquid ને બીજી liquid માં droplets તરીકે distribute કરતો extraction column છે. Repeated droplet formation/contact તથા redistribution થી countercurrent liquids વચ્ચે interfacial transfer વધે છે.

10. Packed Extraction Tower ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Column height દરમિયાન contacting liquids distribute કરવા packing વાપરતો differential extractor છે. Countercurrent liquid flow તથા wetting/droplet renewal discrete equilibrium trays વગર transfer આપે છે.

11. Rotating Disk Contactor (RDC) ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Rotating disks તથા stationary rings ધરાવતો mechanically agitated vertical extraction column છે. Controlled mechanical dispersion interfaces renew કરે છે અને countercurrent flow concentration progression આપે છે.

12. Centrifugal Extractor ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

Liquid–liquid contacting તથા centrifugal acceleration હેઠળ phase separation જોડતું compact contactor છે. Mixing transfer વધારેછે; rotation density-based separation ઝડપી બનાવે છે, પણ પોતે equilibrium selectivity બદલતું નથી.

5. Liquid–Liquid ExtractionMass Transfer-I • DI04005021 • Chemical Semester4 • 10h / 22% • GTU2025-26
Syllabus according to detailed theory, derivations, equipment construction and working and worked numericals. Practicals carry official suggested exercises and blank observation sheets — no fabricated results.
5. Notes
5.1 • Liquid–liquid extraction and industrial uses

Definition / principle

Liquid–liquid extraction separates a dissolved solute by distributing it between the original liquid and another liquid solvent that creates two separable phases. Extract is the solvent-rich product; raffinate is the feed-carrier-rich product.

Detailed theory and conditions

The operation is useful when volatility differences are poor, heat-sensitive materials discourage distillation or a solvent provides useful selectivity. Applications include recovery of organic acids from aqueous streams, purification of selected chemical products and hydrometallurgical extraction using suitable extractants. The solvent normally requires downstream recovery; extraction alone does not necessarily give a pure solute. A light phase is not automatically the extract: which product is extract depends on solvent identity, while top/bottom location depends on density.

5.2 • Liquid equilibrium,distribution and selectivity

Definition / principle

Liquid equilibrium specifies compositions of two coexisting liquid phases at given temperature and pressure. A tie line joins the conjugate equilibrium phase compositions.

Detailed theory and conditions

A distribution coefficient compares solute concentration in extract with that in raffinate on a declared basis. It can vary with composition, temperature and association; it is not universally constant. Selectivity compares separation of solute C from feed carrier A between phases. A solvent with high capacity may also dissolve much carrier and give poor selectivity. There must actually be two phases; one homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture cannot by itself define an interphase distribution coefficient. Water/organic systems need explicitly identified aqueous and organic phases.

Equations and notation

5.3 • Equilateral triangular coordinates and lever rule

Definition / principle

An equilateral ternary composition diagram represents mixtures of three components whose fractions add to one. A vertex represents a pure component and the opposite side represents zero fraction of that component.

Detailed theory and conditions

Read a component fraction along lines parallel to the side opposite its vertex. Always identify component names, temperature and mass or mole basis; do not mix the bases. A binary mixture lies on an edge and a ternary mixture lies inside. A mixing point M for streams F and S lies on their straight joining line, closer to the larger stream. The splitting of M into conjugate E and R lies along a measured tie line, not along an arbitrary line to a vertex. Lever-rule product ratios use opposite segment lengths. Mixing line and equilibrium tie line are different geometric objects.

Equations and notation

5.4 • Three liquids:one partially soluble pair and T/P effects

Definition / principle

A Type-I ternary system has one binary pair with limited mutual solubility, while the third component is mutually miscible with the other two over the stated range.

Detailed theory and conditions

The partially miscible pair creates a miscibility gap whose ternary boundary is the binodal curve. Compositions within the two-phase region split along tie lines; the two branches approach one another at a plait point where the phase distinction disappears. Tie lines are generally not horizontal and their slopes must come from data. For many upper-critical-solution-temperature systems, heating shrinks the miscibility gap, but lower-critical and more complex behavior also exist; do not claim that temperature always increases mutual solubility. Ordinary pressure has a smaller effect on nearly incompressible liquid equilibrium, unless high pressure, gas solubility or special phase behavior is involved. The diagram here is schematic, not measured acetic-acid/benzene/water data.

5.5 • Three liquids:two partially soluble pairs

Definition / principle

A Type-II ternary system has two binary pairs with limited mutual solubility at the specified conditions.

Detailed theory and conditions

Miscibility gaps therefore appear on two binary edges rather than only one. The two-phase region and its conjugate branches must be obtained from equilibrium data; they need not resemble the simple Type-I cap or share its plait-point construction. Tie lines still join coexisting phases and all phase compositions must sum to one. The number of partially miscible binary pairs does not by itself imply three liquid phases. The supplied diagram is a topology sketch identifying the two affected edges, not a source of quantitative stage compositions.

5.6 • Choice of extraction solvent

Definition / principle

An extraction solvent must create a favorable solute distribution and sufficiently separable liquid phases while remaining recoverable and safe.

Detailed theory and conditions

Evaluate selectivity, capacity, mutual solubility with feed carrier, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, chemical stability and ease of regeneration. Adequate density difference helps settling; very stable emulsions or low interfacial tension may hinder disengagement. Low viscosity aids transfer and pumping, but solvent loss/product contamination may still dominate economics. Include toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost and compatibility. A high distribution coefficient alone is insufficient if the solvent is difficult to separate or recover.

5.7 • Derivation:single-stage extraction balance and lever rule

Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady equilibrium stage or completed batch; no reaction/evaporation; F, S, E, R are masses or mass rates on the same basis. zF, zS, zM and wE, wR are solute mass fractions. Equilibrium endpoints must be known independently.

  1. Total balance and mixed composition.

  2. Component balance after phase separation.

  3. Eliminate raffinate flow.

  4. Solve the two product flows.

  5. Rearrange to the lever rule along the E–R tie line.

  6. Also close carrier and solvent balances. A solute-only result is not enough if the assumed ternary endpoints are inconsistent.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: total balance → solute balance → eliminate R → solve E, R; mention measured tie-line endpoints. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

5.8 • Derivation:multistage crosscurrent extraction

Symbols, model and assumptions

First use general stage balances. For the closed-form result assume insoluble carrier flow L remains constant, pure fresh solvent Sj at each stage, negligible mutual solubility and linear equilibrium Yj=mXj on solute-free mass ratios. X=solute/carrier, Y=solute/solvent.

  1. General total and solute balances at stage j.

  2. Write the component balance without assuming constant total raffinate.

  3. Under the stated carrier model, pure solvent has zero entering solute.

  4. Insert the equilibrium ratio and solve.

  5. Successive fresh-solvent contacts multiply the residual factors.

  6. For equal solvent portions and constant m, recovery follows from the residual solute.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: one-stage carrier balance → equilibrium substitution → recurrence → two-stage application. Do not use the simplified formula for mutually soluble ternary phases. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

5.9 • Agitated extraction vessel

Definition

A mechanically mixed vessel that disperses one liquid phase in another to create extraction contact; phase separation completes the stage.

Principle

Agitation increases interfacial area and renews the liquid films so solute moves toward its equilibrium distribution.

Construction

A vessel contains an impeller on a driven shaft, baffles, feed/solvent connections and an outlet for the contacted mixture. A compatible shaft seal and suitable containment limit solvent escape. For batch use the vessel can also allow settling after agitation stops; for continuous use a separate gravity settler normally receives the dispersion. The mixer outlet is therefore a two-phase mixture, not automatically two separated product streams.

Working

Feed and solvent contact under controlled mixing. One phase forms droplets in the other and solute crosses the enlarged interface. Contact continues for the required residence time, but vigorous mixing does not guarantee equilibrium. The dispersion is then settled and the conjugate phases withdrawn separately. Batch operation alternates mixing and settling; continuous mixer–settler operation separates those functions into adjacent units. Excessive shear can produce difficult emulsions and increase carryover.

Applications

Stagewise liquid extraction and a mixer section in mixer–settler cascades.

Limitations and precautions

Power, sealing, emulsification and residence time matter. The hazardous-solvent SOP and rated containment govern actual use.

5.10 • Gravity settler

Definition

A low-velocity vessel separating a contacted liquid dispersion into light and heavy liquid layers by gravity.

Principle

Density difference causes droplets to rise or settle and coalesce when sufficient disengagement time is available.

Construction

A horizontal settling chamber receives dispersion through a calming inlet or baffle. It provides a quiet volume, an interface region and separate light/heavy outlets with level or interface control. Coalescing internals may be provided for a compatible duty, but they do not replace adequate residence time. The diagram labels light and heavy outlets; extract/raffinate identity is assigned according to which layer is solvent-rich.

Working

The mixed dispersion slows on entering the vessel. Droplets migrate under gravity and join their continuous layer, allowing a visible interface to develop. Light liquid leaves above the interface and heavy liquid from below it while outlet arrangements maintain the phase inventory. Settling is a separation step after extraction contact, not a fresh assumption of equilibrium transfer. Fine stable emulsions may remain dispersed and require different contacting/separation conditions rather than simply a higher outlet rate.

Applications

Phase disengagement in mixer–settler extraction and solvent-recovery sections.

Limitations and precautions

Small density difference, high viscosity and emulsions require more area/time. Interface control prevents product cross-contamination.

5.11 • Sieve-tray extraction tower

Definition

A liquid–liquid contact column using perforated trays to distribute one liquid as droplets through the other.

Principle

Repeated droplet formation/contact and phase redistribution increase interfacial transfer between countercurrent liquids.

Construction

The shell carries perforated trays and passages/downcomers for the opposite continuous phase. In the illustrated arrangement, light dispersed solvent enters low and rises through tray holes; heavy feed enters high and passes downward through designated passages. End disengagement sections collect the separated phases with interface controls. Tray spacing and open area govern loading; these are liquid droplets, not gas bubbles as in an absorber.

Working

The light phase issues through perforations and disperses into the heavier continuous liquid. Solute partitions between phases during droplet travel and contact on successive tray levels. Heavy liquid flows downward while the light dispersed phase rises to a top separation zone. The bottom zone withdraws heavy product. Contacting is staged physically but each tray need not be ideal. When the density/continuous-phase choice is reversed, the feed ports and hydraulic arrangement must be redesigned accordingly.

Applications

Countercurrent liquid extraction where tray hydraulics and density difference are suitable.

Limitations and precautions

Flooding, phase inversion, entrainment and emulsion formation limit useful throughput.

5.12 • Packed extraction tower

Definition

A differential liquid–liquid extractor using packing to distribute contacting phases over the column height.

Principle

Countercurrent liquid flow and repeated wetting/droplet renewal provide interfacial transfer without discrete equilibrium trays.

Construction

A vertical shell contains compatible packing, supports, phase distributors and enlarged end disengagement zones. For the illustrated light-solvent case, heavy feed enters above the bed and light solvent below it. Light and heavy outlets have interface control. Packing wetting and continuous/dispersed-phase choice must suit the actual liquids; the arrangement is not a gas absorber merely with its stream names changed.

Working

Light solvent moves upward through the packing while the heavy liquid flows downward. The distributed phases exchange solute along the bed and then disengage at the ends. In the stated example, the solvent-rich extract leaves from the light end and carrier-rich raffinate from the heavy end, but this product positioning reverses if solvent density reverses. Maldistribution reduces useful area, and excessive loading causes entrainment, flooding or phase inversion rather than guaranteed better transfer.

Applications

Continuous extraction with sufficiently clean liquids and favorable distribution/wetting.

Limitations and precautions

Fouling, emulsions, poor wetting and small density difference can make the duty unsuitable.

5.13 • Rotating disk contactor (RDC)

Definition

A mechanically agitated vertical extraction column with rotating disks and stationary rings.

Principle

Controlled mechanical dispersion renews liquid interfaces while countercurrent flow provides the concentration progression.

Construction

The column contains a central driven shaft carrying spaced circular disks and a shell fitted with stationary ring baffles. The contacting section has feed/solvent inlets, while top and bottom disengagement zones provide separated outlets and interface control. A motor and suitable shaft seal drive the rotor. The stator rings divide circulation regions and limit excessive axial mixing; the disks are not perforated equilibrium trays.

Working

The rotor shears and circulates the liquid phases to form useful droplets and renew their surrounding films. Heavy and light streams move countercurrently through successive agitated regions while solute partitions between them. The end zones slow the dispersion so phases separate before withdrawal. Rotor speed affects droplet size, holdup, power and axial mixing; increasing speed indefinitely can cause emulsification or flooding rather than improved separation. The column still requires actual equilibrium data and residence-time/efficiency information.

Applications

Continuous liquid extraction requiring controlled mechanical dispersion.

Limitations and precautions

Moving parts, seals, power, axial mixing and emulsion sensitivity require suitable design/maintenance.

5.14 • Centrifugal extractor

Definition

A compact contactor that combines liquid–liquid contacting with phase separation under centrifugal acceleration.

Principle

Mixing promotes solute transfer; rotation accelerates density-based phase separation without changing the equilibrium selectivity by itself.

Construction

A representative unit has a stationary housing, two liquid feeds, a mixing region, a rotating separating bowl and separate outlets controlled by internal weirs or passages. A motor, shaft, bearings and appropriate seals support the rotor. The schematic distinguishes the heavy outer layer from the lighter inner layer; exact inlet/rotor arrangements vary by design. These devices need balanced rotating assemblies and rated containment.

Working

Feed and solvent first form a contacted dispersion, allowing solute to approach its distribution relation. The mixture enters the rotating separation zone, where the denser liquid moves outward and the lighter liquid inward. Each layer follows its designated outlet path, producing separate phases rapidly compared with gravity settling alone. A single centrifugal unit is not automatically many ideal stages; multiple units may be cascaded for greater recovery or purity. Excessive solids, unstable hydraulics or poor mixing can still limit performance.

Applications

Compact extraction, short residence-time duties and difficult gravity disengagement when the fluids suit the rotor design.

Limitations and precautions

Rotor balance, speed rating, seals, power and solids tolerance matter; never infer safe operating limits from an educational sketch.

5.16 • Numerical:two-stage crosscurrent extraction

Given

Formula

Final answer with units

Validity check

Solved numericals and practicals
Single-stage extraction efficiency

Objective and official scope

Measure actual extraction and compare it with an explicitly defined ideal-stage reference at the same inputs, temperature and basis. Keep recovery distinct from stage efficiency.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved immiscible feed/solvent pair, sealed contacting/settling apparatus, balance, temperature measurement and calibrated solute assay. Equilibrium endpoints/reference must be supplied or independently established.

Principle and assumptions

Use measured phase masses and solute fractions for product solute balances. The mixer must be followed by phase separation.

Procedure and record

Record feed and solvent masses, compositions, temperature, contact/settling conditions and both separated product masses/assays. Identify solvent-rich extract and carrier-rich raffinate rather than assigning names solely from layer position. Determine actual recovered solute and compare with the provided ideal reference. Account for holdup and samples.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Use closed approved solvent handling and ventilation. Do not report recovery as efficiency without the ideal reference. No invented equilibrium compositions or observations.

Objective and official scope

Measure actual extraction and compare it with an explicitly defined ideal-stage reference at the same inputs, temperature and basis. Keep recovery distinct from stage efficiency.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved immiscible feed/solvent pair, sealed contacting/settling apparatus, balance, temperature measurement and calibrated solute assay. Equilibrium endpoints/reference must be supplied or independently established.

Principle and assumptions

Use measured phase masses and solute fractions for product solute balances. Each raffinate is contacted with a new solvent portion; extracts are collected separately.

Procedure and record

Record feed and solvent masses, compositions, temperature, contact/settling conditions and both separated product masses/assays. Repeat with the first raffinate and a separately recorded fresh solvent portion. Determine actual recovered solute and compare with the provided ideal reference. Account for holdup and samples.

Preparation of a ternary diagram

Objective and official scope

Construct the binodal data for the approved three-liquid system at a recorded temperature.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved ternary liquids, closed vessels, precision balance, temperature control and cloud-point/assay method specified by the laboratory.

Principle and assumptions

The three measured mass fractions sum to1. Cloud points define a miscibility boundary; they do not alone provide every tie line.

Procedure and record

Follow the approved cloud-point protocol on several prepared composition paths. Record cumulative masses and temperature at each valid persistent-cloud transition, calculate fractions and plot on a labelled equilateral diagram. Repeat checks near uncertain transitions and identify the single/two-phase sides. Do not copy schematic points as experimental data.

Tie-line data:acetic acid–benzene–water

Objective and official scope

Obtain conjugate liquid compositions for the exact syllabus system only where institutionally approved; otherwise use an explicitly labelled approved substitute/demonstration.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved closed equilibrium/settling apparatus, temperature control, balance, validated acid assay and sufficient composition calibration/binodal data to identify all three component fractions.

Principle and assumptions

A measured tie line joins the two phases after equilibrium at the same T/P. An acid assay alone is only one independent composition measurement; use validated additional information to locate full ternary endpoints.

Procedure and record

Under the approved protocol prepare and equilibrate known mixtures, allow clear phase separation and sample each layer without cross-contamination. Assay acid and use the validated composition method/binodal branch to obtain full phase compositions. Plot conjugate endpoints and join them. Check total/component balance including sampled quantities. Record sources/calibration and actual observations.

Safety, quality and limitations

Distribution coefficient:toluene/acetic-acid and chloroform/acetic-acid systems

Objective and official scope

Determine acid distribution using the laboratory-confirmed two-phase systems. The printed title omits the other phase; confirm it before any test.

Apparatus and preparation

Institution-approved phase pairs and assays; commonly an aqueous acid phase and the selected organic solvent are considered in separate experiments, but the laboratory manual must confirm the actual composition and method.

Principle and assumptions

Toluene mixed only with acetic acid or chloroform mixed only with acetic acid must not automatically be assumed to form two liquid phases. A distribution coefficient needs identified coexisting phases and a declared concentration basis.

Procedure and record

Follow the approved equilibrium/settling and sampling method. Assay acid in both phases at recorded temperature and calculate KD on the same mass-fraction or molar-concentration basis for every sample. Compare values versus overall composition and report if the constant-distribution approximation fails. Do not infer a missing aqueous phase without confirming the manual.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Toluene is flammable and chloroform is toxic; approved ventilation, closed handling, segregated waste and supervised SOP are mandatory. No mixing recipe or fabricated data is supplied.

Viva questions
1. Define and explain the principle of Liquid–liquid extraction and industrial uses.

Liquid–liquid extraction separates a dissolved solute by distributing it between the original liquid and another liquid solvent that creates two separable phases. Extract is the solvent-rich product; raffinate is the feed-carrier-rich product. The operation is useful when volatility differences are poor, heat-sensitive materials discourage distillation or a solvent provides useful selectivity. Applications include recovery of organic acids from aqueous streams, purification of selected chemical products and hydrometallurgical extraction using suitable extractants. The solvent normally requires downstream recovery; extraction alone does not necessarily give a pure solute. A light phase is not automatically the extract: which product is extract depends on solvent identity, while top/bottom location depends on density.

2. Define and explain the principle of Liquid equilibrium,distribution and selectivity.

Liquid equilibrium specifies compositions of two coexisting liquid phases at given temperature and pressure. A tie line joins the conjugate equilibrium phase compositions. A distribution coefficient compares solute concentration in extract with that in raffinate on a declared basis. It can vary with composition, temperature and association; it is not universally constant. Selectivity compares separation of solute C from feed carrier A between phases. A solvent with high capacity may also dissolve much carrier and give poor selectivity. There must actually be two phases; one homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture cannot by itself define an interphase distribution coefficient. Water/organic systems need explicitly identified aqueous and organic phases.

3. Define and explain the principle of Equilateral triangular coordinates and lever rule.

An equilateral ternary composition diagram represents mixtures of three components whose fractions add to one. A vertex represents a pure component and the opposite side represents zero fraction of that component. Read a component fraction along lines parallel to the side opposite its vertex. Always identify component names, temperature and mass or mole basis; do not mix the bases. A binary mixture lies on an edge and a ternary mixture lies inside. A mixing point M for streams F and S lies on their straight joining line, closer to the larger stream. The splitting of M into conjugate E and R lies along a measured tie line, not along an arbitrary line to a vertex. Lever-rule product ratios use opposite segment lengths. Mixing line and equilibrium tie line are different geometric objects.

4. Define and explain the principle of Three liquids:one partially soluble pair and T/P effects.

A Type-I ternary system has one binary pair with limited mutual solubility, while the third component is mutually miscible with the other two over the stated range. The partially miscible pair creates a miscibility gap whose ternary boundary is the binodal curve. Compositions within the two-phase region split along tie lines; the two branches approach one another at a plait point where the phase distinction disappears. Tie lines are generally not horizontal and their slopes must come from data. For many upper-critical-solution-temperature systems, heating shrinks the miscibility gap, but lower-critical and more complex behavior also exist; do not claim that temperature always increases mutual solubility. Ordinary pressure has a smaller effect on nearly incompressible liquid equilibrium, unless high pressure, gas solubility or special phase behavior is involved. The diagram here is schematic, not measured acetic-acid/benzene/water data.

5. Define and explain the principle of Three liquids:two partially soluble pairs.

A Type-II ternary system has two binary pairs with limited mutual solubility at the specified conditions. Miscibility gaps therefore appear on two binary edges rather than only one. The two-phase region and its conjugate branches must be obtained from equilibrium data; they need not resemble the simple Type-I cap or share its plait-point construction. Tie lines still join coexisting phases and all phase compositions must sum to one. The number of partially miscible binary pairs does not by itself imply three liquid phases. The supplied diagram is a topology sketch identifying the two affected edges, not a source of quantitative stage compositions.

6. Define and explain the principle of Choice of extraction solvent.

An extraction solvent must create a favorable solute distribution and sufficiently separable liquid phases while remaining recoverable and safe. Evaluate selectivity, capacity, mutual solubility with feed carrier, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, chemical stability and ease of regeneration. Adequate density difference helps settling; very stable emulsions or low interfacial tension may hinder disengagement. Low viscosity aids transfer and pumping, but solvent loss/product contamination may still dominate economics. Include toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost and compatibility. A high distribution coefficient alone is insufficient if the solvent is difficult to separate or recover.

7. Define and explain the principle of Agitated extraction vessel.

A mechanically mixed vessel that disperses one liquid phase in another to create extraction contact; phase separation completes the stage. Agitation increases interfacial area and renews the liquid films so solute moves toward its equilibrium distribution.

8. Define and explain the principle of Gravity settler.

A low-velocity vessel separating a contacted liquid dispersion into light and heavy liquid layers by gravity. Density difference causes droplets to rise or settle and coalesce when sufficient disengagement time is available.

9. Define and explain the principle of Sieve-tray extraction tower.

A liquid–liquid contact column using perforated trays to distribute one liquid as droplets through the other. Repeated droplet formation/contact and phase redistribution increase interfacial transfer between countercurrent liquids.

10. Define and explain the principle of Packed extraction tower.

A differential liquid–liquid extractor using packing to distribute contacting phases over the column height. Countercurrent liquid flow and repeated wetting/droplet renewal provide interfacial transfer without discrete equilibrium trays.

11. Define and explain the principle of Rotating disk contactor (RDC).

A mechanically agitated vertical extraction column with rotating disks and stationary rings. Controlled mechanical dispersion renews liquid interfaces while countercurrent flow provides the concentration progression.

12. Define and explain the principle of Centrifugal extractor.

A compact contactor that combines liquid–liquid contacting with phase separation under centrifugal acceleration. Mixing promotes solute transfer; rotation accelerates density-based phase separation without changing the equilibrium selectivity by itself.
